# mesh-build — DSH plugin for volume-mesh building

Four tools for the `Mesh_3D_pore_scale` project: meshing routes (snappyHexMesh, cfMesh, gmsh route D),
scaffolding a runnable snappy case from an STL, a quality verdict against the project thresholds, and
delivery as two distributions (an OpenFOAM case + a Fluent `.msh`). Every command is a real
OpenFOAM/cfMesh command on this machine, the logs stay on disk, and a short summary goes into the response.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Arguments |
|---|---|---|
| `mesh_hints` | knowledge cards: snappy, cfMesh/pMesh, gmsh route D, the gate, delivery, rejected routes | `query`, `id`, `limit` |
| `mesh_build` | route + case scaffold + gate | `route`, `caseDir`, `scaffold`, `stl`, `scaffoldOptions`, `np`, `splitRegions`, `gate`, `profile`, `minVol`, `overwrite`, `skipBlockMesh`, `dryRun`, `gmshScript`, `gmshArgs`, `msh` |
| `mesh_check` | JS gate per region; writes `mesh-passport.json`, leaves the mesh untouched | `caseDir`, `regions`, `profile`, `minVol` |
| `mesh_deliver` | delivery of a gate-passing mesh: OF case + `.tar.gz`, Fluent `.msh` + `.zip`, a report with the checks | `caseDir`, `name`, `outDir`, `gateProfile`, `minVol`, `regions`, `multiRegion`, `noCombinedMesh`, `skipAnsys`, `keepScratch`, `force`, `dryRun` |
| `mesh_capabilities` | What this installation accepts: distribution/version, executables (cfMesh, gmsh, …) and the dictionary keys read from `$WM_PROJECT_DIR/etc/caseDicts/annotated` (`scale` vs `convertToMeters`, `minMedialAxisAngle` vs `minMedianAxisAngle`, `locationsInMesh`) | `openfoam`, `refresh` |
| `mesh_first_layer` | y+ → layer sizing (flat plate: Cf, u_τ, first layer, δ, layer count) with a ready `scaffoldOptions` block; or the inverse: a known first layer → its y+ | `uRef`, `lRef`, `nu`, `yPlusTarget`, `expansionRatio`, `coverage`, `cellSize`, `layerSurfaces`, `firstLayer`, `caseDir` |
| `mesh_surface_check` | Fidelity of the built surface vs the reference STL: exports the patch faces from `constant/polyMesh` (JS, no OpenFOAM utility needed) and compares bbox, volume, area and an approximate Hausdorff; catches a domain that clips the geometry | `caseDir`, `stl`, `patches`, `region`, `tol`, `samples`, `keepStl` |
| `mesh_patch_types` | solver roles for existing patches (retype `boundary`, `.bak` + diff, updates `handoff.json`) | `caseDir`, `roles`, `region`, `dryRun`, `recheck`, `profile`, `minVol` |
| `mesh_revise` | plan A3: a `mesh-feedback/1` document becomes the next revision (advice table as data, rebuild + re-gate + history) | `caseDir`, `feedback`, `feedbackFile`, `attempt`, `apply`, `profile`, `minVol`, `np` |


## Description and topics

**Description** (`package.json` → `description`): volume meshes for the pore scale — snappyHexMesh
(hex-dominant, layers, multi-region CHT), cfMesh cartesianMesh, gmsh OCC conformal route D, checkMesh and a
strict quality gate per region with correct handling of the absolute `minVol`.

**Topics** (`package.json` → `keywords`): `openfoam`, `snappyhexmesh`, `cfmesh`, `gmsh`, `volume-mesh`,
`cht`, `quality-gate`, `checkmesh`, `pore-scale`, `minvol`.

**For the chat**: the tool `description`s in `index.js`, `description` + `whenToUse` in `lib/skill.js`, the
`plugin-mesh-build` card in `data/hints/plugin.json`; its `topics` = `keywords`.

Without `route` the tool lists routes, profiles and steps; without `query`, `mesh_hints` returns the card catalog.

## Installation

```json
{ "action": "install_bundle", "target": "<absolute path to the repository>/plugins/mesh-build" }
```

Substitute your own path — DSH accepts only an absolute one (`$(pwd)/plugins/mesh-build` from the project root).

This is the DSH `plugin_manager` tool (it requires confirmation): it adds a `link:` to the profile and
enables the bundle, so edits in `plugins/mesh-build/` are visible to the live session. Re-activation after
edits: `plugin_manager({ "action": "set_plugin", "target": "include:mesh-build" })`.
A check without DSH:

```bash
node plugins/mesh-build/scripts/smoke.mjs   # config, routes, cards, scaffold into tmp, serial/parallel plan
```

Requirements: Node ≥ 20, DSH `>= 0.2.2-rc.1 < 0.3.0`, OpenFOAM (ESI v2512; `etc/bashrc` is looked up in the
standard installation directories, an explicit path comes from `openfoamBashrc`/`MESH_BUILD_OPENFOAM_BASHRC`),
`tools/qa/mesh_gate.sh`, `tools/deliver/make_delivery.sh`, `mpirun` for parallel meshing.

## Configuration

```json
// ~/.config/mesh-build/config.json   (or $MESH_BUILD_CONFIG=/path/config.json)
{
  "projectRoot": "/path/to/Mesh_3D_pore_scale",
  "caseRoot": "cases",
  "workRoot": ".cache/mesh-build",
  "np": 6,
  "timeoutMs": 1800000
}
```

`projectRoot` can be omitted — it is searched upwards from the agent's working directory; `caseRoot`/`workRoot`
are paths **relative** to the project root (without a profile — relative to the current directory, `caseRoot`
defaults to `cases`).

Variables: `MESH_BUILD_PROJECT_ROOT`, `MESH_BUILD_PYTHON`, `MESH_BUILD_WORK_ROOT`,
`MESH_BUILD_CASE_ROOT`, `MESH_BUILD_NP`, `MESH_BUILD_TIMEOUT_MS`, `MESH_BUILD_CONFIG`,
`MESH_BUILD_OPENFOAM_BASHRC` and `MESH_BUILD_OPENFOAM_ROOTS` (extra installation directories, colon-separated).

## Routes (`data/engine.json`)

| route | steps | when |
|---|---|---|
| `snappy` | blockMesh → surfaceFeatureExtract → (decomposePar → snappy -parallel → reconstruct) or snappy serial → splitMeshRegions | pore STLs, CHT by `cellZones`, hex-dominant + layers |
| `cfmesh` | clean → decomposePar → cartesianMesh -parallel → reconstruct → clean processors (or serial) | a robust hex mesh when snapping is unstable |
| `gmsh` | `<python> <gmshScript> <gmshArgs>` → `gmshToFoam <msh> -case <case>` → splitMeshRegions | conformal CHT from OCC (route D) |
| `check` | — | only check an existing case |

The steps are declarative: `{ name, run, when, timeoutMs }`, `when` ∈ `always | blockMesh | features | parallel |
serial | splitRegions`. Placeholders: `{caseDir} {np} {msh} {python} {gmshScript} {gmshArgs}`. Logs go to
`<caseDir>/logs/plugin-<route>-NN-<step>.log`; on failure the response returns `failedStep` and `troubleshooting`
from the route's `failures`.

## The snappy scaffold

`mesh_build({ scaffold: true, stl: [...], scaffoldOptions: {...} })` writes a verified case:

- `system/{blockMeshDict,snappyHexMeshDict,meshQualityDict,surfaceFeatureExtractDict,decomposeParDict,controlDict,fvSchemes,fvSolution}`, `0/.keep`;
- the case is in **metres** (`convertToMeters 1`), the project STL in **mm** — `scale 0.001` is added to `geometry{}`;
- the outer domain boundary is `symmetry` (otherwise snapping moves points off the plane, exp-006/D-013);
- `locationsInMesh` from `locationInMesh`: `[x,y,z]` or `[{point:[x,y,z], name:"fluid"}]`, multi-region → `cellZones` → `splitMeshRegions`;
- `minVol` is absolute (`1e-14` by default, the rule `h_min³/6`), `maxNonOrtho` 65 in `meshQualityDict`;
- layers only for the listed `layerSurfaces`;
- if `locationInMesh` lands inside a closed solid body, the build stops (`phase: "sanity"`,
  "no `world` patch") — pick the point with `scripts/fluid-point.py`
  (`<python> scripts/fluid-point.py model.stl --clearance 0.1`).

`scaffoldOptions`: `domainMin`, `domainMax` (metres), `cells` or `cellSize` (metres), `locationInMesh`,
`refinementLevels {surface:level}`, `defaultLevel`, `layerSurfaces`, `nLayers`, `layerThickness`,
`minThickness`, `symmetryDomain`, `minVol`, `maxNonOrtho`, `resolveFeatureAngle`.

### Domain sizing without typing a box

Instead of `domainMin`/`domainMax` you can let the scaffold derive the box from the STL bounding box:

```js
scaffoldOptions: { domain: { type: "external" }, targetCells: 60000, locationInMesh: [-0.01, 0, 0] }
```

- `type: "external"` — multiples of `L` = the largest STL extent: upstream 3·L, downstream 5·L, lateral 3·L,
  vertical 3·L below and above (`flowAxis: "x"` by default). `type: "internal"` is the bbox itself,
  `type: "wrap"` pads 0.1·L on every side. Margins and `sizeFactor` override the multiples.
- Explicit `domainMin`/`domainMax` always win — the answer then carries a warning that the mode was ignored.
- `targetCells` picks the background cell size from the domain volume (`(V/targetCells)^(1/3)`); the answer
  says which cell size it used, and `cells: [nx,ny,nz]` still wins when given.
- **Unit suspicion**: if the inferred domain's STL bbox is wider than 100 mm, `mesh_build` answers `needs_input`
  ("is this file in millimetres?") instead of quietly building a 1000× too large box. `assumeUnits: "mm"`, an
  explicit domain, or a smaller model continues without asking.

Measured: sphere r5 with `domain {type:"external"}` and `targetCells 60000` → box −35…55 × ±35 mm,
47×37×37 background cells, snappy builds, gate PASS. A 40×20×20 mm box with `targetCells 16000` → 1.0 mm cells,
`cells [40,20,20]`.

## Shared core and passports

The gate, the `checkMesh` parser, config, paths, cards and the `mesh-handoff/1` writer live in `../sim-core`;
this plugin is a provider of the `simMesh` service (`build`/`check`/`deliver`/`patchTypes`/`hints`), a provider of
the `meshToolkit` service (`mesh`/`gate`/`deliver`/`patchTypes`) and a consumer of `simHints`.
The project profile is `sim-project.json` at the root (units, caseRoots, scratch, foam, gate, geometry, cores).
After a scaffold `case-manifest.json` is written, after the gate — `mesh-passport.json`:
route, cells, regions, gate, sha256/size/mtime of the polyMesh. `mesh_check` reports passport freshness
and any mismatch between the recorded verdict and the current one.

## Quality gate

`mesh_check` (and automatically after a successful `mesh_build` when `gate` ≠ false) calls the JS gate
`sim-core/lib/gate.js`: it writes the complete `meshQualityDict` (13 keys), builds the overlay
`<case>/.mesh-gate/<target>` and runs `checkMesh -meshQuality`. The verdict is computed **from the text**:
`checkMesh` returns 0 even on `Failed N mesh checks`. Result:
`{ verdict: PASS|FAIL|ERROR, failingRegions, results[{target, pass, failKind, metrics}] }`, where `metrics` are
`cells`, `maxNonOrtho`, `avgNonOrtho`, `maxSkewness`, `minVolume`, `violations`, layers
(`Added N out of M cells (P%)`). `minVol` is absolute: not set by the profile/call → `-1` is written into the
dictionary (check disabled) and the response carries `disabled-minVol-not-configured`; on failure — the advice
`minVol = minVolume/12`. `gate.engine: "script"` + `gate.script` is kept as an escape hatch to
`tools/qa/mesh_gate.sh`.

## Capabilities (`mesh_capabilities`)

One probe answers what the installation really accepts — and the scaffold follows it, so no dictionary key is
guessed from a version number:

```js
mesh_capabilities({ openfoam: "com2606" })
// summary: "OpenFOAM v2606 (com) · cfMesh yes · gmsh yes · features dict surfaceFeatureExtractDict ·
//           layer key minMedialAxisAngle · blockMesh key scale"
```

The probe reads two independent sources because either one alone lies: the executables (cfMesh is OpenCFD-only,
`surfaceFeatures` is Foundation-only) and the annotated case dictionaries shipped with the build (they carry the key
spelling of *this* build, which a version table cannot know for a patched release). The result is cached per bashrc;
`refresh: true` re-reads it. `mesh_build` returns the same block as `caps`.

## Surface fidelity (`mesh_surface_check`)

Snappy may silently drop half of the geometry when `domainMin`/`domainMax` cut the STL — the gate still says PASS
because the mesh it kept is fine. This tool compares the meshed surface with the reference STL:

```js
mesh_surface_check({ caseDir: "cases/sphere", stl: ["stl/sphere.clean.stl"], tol: 0.05 })
// -> { verdict: "PASS", diffs: { bboxRel: 0.0002, areaRel: 0.002, volRel: 0.0002, hausdorffRel: 0.0005 }, faces: 1848 }
```

- The patch surface is exported from `constant/polyMesh/{points,faces,boundary}` in JS: `surfaceMeshTriangulate`
  exists only in OpenFOAM.org, and the pointer needs no OpenFOAM at all.
- Reference STL units come from `handoff.json` (`units.stl`, millimetres by default) and are converted to metres.
- **PASS = `bboxRel <= tol` and `hausdorffRel <= tol`.** Area and volume are diagnostics: a snapped voxel surface is
  stair-stepped, so a sphere legitimately has `areaRel ≈ 0.46` while its Hausdorff stays under 1 %.
- The Hausdorff is approximate — triangle centroids of one surface against the triangles of the other (uniform grid,
  expanding-ring queries, both directions), which is fast and catches clipping, not sub-micron ripples.
- A FAIL with `bboxRel > tol` means the domain clips the geometry: enlarge it (or use `domain: { type: "external" }`).

## First layer from y+ (`mesh_first_layer`)

Size the near wall before meshing, instead of guessing `nLayers`/`firstLayerThickness`:

```
mesh_first_layer({ uRef: 30, lRef: 5, nu: 1.5e-5, yPlusTarget: 1, caseDir: "cases/sphere" })
```

The calculator uses the flat-plate correlation `Cf = 0.026·Re^(-1/7)`, `u_τ = U·√(Cf/2)`, first layer
`y⁺·ν/u_τ`, boundary layer `δ = 0.37·L·Re^(-0.2)`, and covers `coverage·δ` with geometric growth. It returns the
dimensionless numbers, the absolute dimensions, the layer count and a `scaffoldOptions` block for `mesh_build`.

**Relative vs absolute:** the snappy scaffold writes `relativeSizes true`, so `layerThickness` is relative to the
near-wall cell. Pass `cellSize` (metres, after refinement) — or `caseDir`, and the tool reads it from
`handoff.json` or from `blockMeshDict` + `polyMesh/points` + the refinement levels. With an absolute thickness
snappy quietly removes every layer (`Extruding 0 out of N faces`), which is exactly what this tool prevents; it
warns when the relative final layer would fall below `minThickness 0.075`.

Inverse mode answers the other question — "this mesh has a 5 µm first layer, what y+ does that give?":

```
mesh_first_layer({ uRef: 30, lRef: 5, firstLayer: 5e-6 })
```

`mesh_revise`'s `yplus` category uses the same correlation (`lib/firstlayer.js`), so a hand calculation and the
automatic revision cannot disagree.

## Patch roles (`mesh_patch_types`)

A scaffolded snappy case gives two patches: the obstacle/box faces as `wall` and the outer domain box as
`symmetry` (`world`). A solver needs flow roles, and in a regional case `changeDictionary` does not work, so the
type is retyped in `constant/<region>/polyMesh/boundary` (AGENTS.md §13, exp-006/D-013). `mesh_patch_types` does
that edit: it rewrites only the `type` line of each named patch, keeps `<boundary>.bak`, returns the before/after
diff, and refuses what it cannot do safely — an unknown patch name (listing the available `name (type)`), one
patch in two roles, `empty`/`cyclic`/`cyclicAMI` as a target for a flow boundary (topological constraints),
`cyclic`/`wedge` without a neighbour patch or wedge geometry, a multi-region case without `region`, and splitting
one patch into inlet+outlet (that needs a face set: `topoSet` + `createPatch`, or named patches from the
geometry). Inlet and outlet end up as type `patch`, so the semantic role is stored in `handoff.json` and carried
forward by `mesh_check`. `recheck:true` re-runs the gate and reports `sameAsRecorded` — patch types change what a
solver reads, never the mesh metrics. After a retype the passport is stale: run `mesh_check` again before
`mesh_deliver`.

## Revision loop (`mesh_revise`)

A solver run sends back a `mesh-feedback/1` document (category, evidence, expected values). `mesh_revise`
does not guess: the reaction table is **data** in `data/advice.json` — every category has a ladder of ops and a
ceiling, and the tool applies the NEXT rung, counted from the `revision` entries already in `handoff.json`.

- `apply:false` (default) returns the plan: which op, why, and the parameters that would change.
- `apply:true` rebuilds with `mesh_build` (same STL, domain, levels and minVol from the handoff), re-runs
  `mesh_check`, and appends `{attempt, category, changes, verdict}` to `history[]`.
- `patch-roles` goes through `mesh_patch_types` (no rebuild). `stl-quality` stops and asks for `stl_check` +
  cleanup. `units` refuses without an explicit `scale`.
- After three consecutive `nonortho`/`skewness` failures the table switches the strategy once
  (snappy → cfmesh) instead of repeating parameters; at the ceiling the tool returns
  `{ok:false, escalated:true, options:[...]}` for the user to choose.

The `yplus` rung computes `firstLayer = yPlus·ν/uTau` (the same correlation as `compute_first_layer`), derives the
layer count from the target first layer and the local cell size, and lowers snappy's own `minVol` threshold to
`firstLayer³/6` — otherwise snappy removes every layer before the gate ever sees it (benchmark DEF-10).

## OpenFOAM versions

Installations are declared in `sim-project.json` (`foam.installations`, `foam.default`); the tools accept
`openfoam: "<id>"` or an absolute path to `etc/bashrc`. Without the argument the default installation is used.

| | OpenFOAM.com (v2412…v2606) | OpenFOAM.org (v14) |
|---|---|---|
| cfMesh (`cartesianMesh`, `pMesh`, …) | ✅ | ❌ |
| `surfaceFeatureExtract` | ✅ | stub |
| `surfaceFeatures` + `surfaceFeaturesDict` | ❌ | ✅ |
| `reconstructParMesh -mergeTol` | ✅ | ❌ |
| `locationsInMesh` (multi-region CHT) | ✅ | ❌ |
| `foamRun` / `foamMultiRun` | ❌ | ✅ |

The `snappy` route adapts itself (choice of the feature dictionary, the `-mergeTol` flag); `preflight` of the
`cfmesh` route refuses outright on org. Verified on a 10 mm cube: com2512/com2606 — `maxNonOrtho 9.7073°`,
org14 — `25.2146°` with the same 2584 cells (`experiments/exp-019_openfoam-version-matrix`).
Details and installation — `meshing/OPENFOAM_VERSIONS.md`.

## Delivery (`mesh_deliver`)

`mesh_deliver` calls `make_delivery.sh` and returns a short JSON instead of the log. The script is taken from
the project (`tools/deliver/make_delivery.sh`), and if it is missing — from the bundle (`scripts/deliver/`, plan 1.4);
the chosen source is visible in `scriptOrigin`:

- **OpenFOAM**: `openfoam_<name>/` with a real `constant/` (`polyMesh`, `triSurface`), `system/`, `0/`,
  the `<name>.foam` marker (opens in ParaView) and a `.tar.gz` archive.
- **ANSYS/Fluent**: `ansys_<name>/<name>.msh`, the `read_mesh.jou` journal, a `.zip` archive; for CHT — one `.msh`
  per region, the base goes to `constant/polyMesh_combined`.
- **Report**: `delivery_<name>.{json,md}` — cells/patches/volume, the `.msh` → OpenFOAM round-trip,
  interface adjacency, the gate verdict.

The script verifies everything by actually running it: `checkMesh` inside the packaged case, the `<a>_to_<b>` ↔
`<b>_to_<a>` interface by face count, the sum of region volumes against combined, the round-trip through
`fluentMeshToFoam`/`fluent3DMeshToFoam`, the strict gate per region and archive integrity.

Precondition — a fresh `mesh-passport.json`: without a passport the tool returns `passport-missing`,
with a modified polyMesh — `passport-stale`; `force: true` lifts the restriction (the delivery gate still
runs). Pass `minVol` explicitly — otherwise the script uses its own `1e-14` threshold, which is too large for pore
cells of 0.05–0.1 mm. Example:

```json
{"caseDir":"experiments/exp-018_snappy-parameter-study/cases/v13_best",
 "name":"cht_v13","minVol":1e-16,"outDir":"deliver"}
```

Result (verified): multi-region 575 757 cells, the interface matches, both regions PASS,
round-trip ok, 66.6 s; single-region FCC — 27 424 cells, 3.5 s.

## Portable mode (without `sim-project.json`)

The tools work in an empty directory: the response carries `project: "defaults"` and `configured: false`,
cases default to `./cases`, the gate profile is `project`, and `mesh_deliver` uses the bundled copy of
`scripts/deliver/make_delivery.sh` (the gate writes its overlay into `<outDir>/.gate`).
The end-to-end scenario STL → snappy → gate → delivery and the table of default values —
[`docs/PORTABLE.md`](docs/PORTABLE.md); card `mesh_hints({ id: "portable-mesh-build" })`.

## Knowledge cards (`data/hints/`)

`snappy.json` (10) — parameter traps; `cfmesh-gmsh.json` (4) — cartesianMesh/pMesh/layers over tetra/route D;
`quality.json` (7) — the gate, absolute minVol, delivery, polyhedra, ParaView, rejected routes, Fluent.

## Extending

- **A route**: an entry in `data/engine.json` (steps + `failures` with verbatim error strings). Removing the entry
  removes the route from the tool.
- **Knowledge**: a card in `data/hints/*.json` (see the format in mesh-stl/README).
- **The case template**: `lib/scaffold.js` (`writeSnappyCase`) — the only place where dictionaries are written;
  change it together with `node plugins/mesh-build/scripts/smoke.mjs`.
- After edits — smoke and a bundle reload: `plugin_manager set_plugin {target:"include:mesh-build",
  enabled:false}` → `enabled:true`. Changed ESM modules are unloaded on reload; no DSH restart is needed.

## Limits

- It does not build geometry (that is `mesh-stl`) and does not run solvers.
- Long runs go to the background: the tool returns control at the step's `timeoutMs`, the full log stays on disk.
- An existing case is not overwritten without `overwrite: true`; `mesh_check` does not change the mesh but writes `mesh-passport.json`.

# dsh-mesh-toolkit

[![ci](https://github.com/AstDen/dsh-mesh-toolkit/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/AstDen/dsh-mesh-toolkit/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

> **0.7.4** · packages: mesh-build 0.7.4 · mesh-stl 0.4.1 · sim-core 0.5.1
> host-only plugins distilled from the `Mesh_3D_pore_scale` project. Build a
> watertight STL, turn it into a checked OpenFOAM mesh, then package it as an
> OpenFOAM case plus an ANSYS/Fluent `.msh`. Seven tools, 21–35 searchable knowledge
> cards per catalog, no build step. Meshing routes adapt to OpenFOAM.com **or** OpenFOAM.org.
> Every checked case carries a `handoff.json` (schema `mesh-handoff/1`) for a solver-side workbench,
> and the optional `meshToolkit` service (`apiVersion: 1`) lets one call mesh, gate and deliver.

| Package | Jobs | Tools |
|---|---|---|
| [`sim-core/`](sim-core/) | config layering, `sim-project.json`, path resolver, checkMesh parser, JS quality gate, passports, shared cards | library, no tools |
| [`mesh-stl/`](mesh-stl/) | STL families and portable primitives, in-plugin JS contract QA (python `stl_qa.py` as parity reference), cleanup, passport row | `stl_hints` · `stl_generate` · `stl_check` |
| [`mesh-build/`](mesh-build/) | snappyHexMesh / cfMesh / gmsh route D on any OpenFOAM build, JS quality gate, mesh passport, OF+Fluent delivery | `mesh_hints` · `mesh_build` · `mesh_check` · `mesh_deliver` |

Thin wrappers over the project's real generators and OpenFOAM binaries. No invented
metrics: every number comes from a real run, full logs stay on disk, the tool returns
a compact JSON summary. Plugins talk to each other through Cordis services
(`simHints`, `simGeometry`, `simMesh`), not through each other's files.

## Status

Validated on **OpenFOAM.com v2512**, **v2606** and **OpenFOAM.org v14**, **ParaView 6.2.1**,
**gmsh 4.15.2**, **CadQuery 2.8.0**, Node 24.

**9 tools · 39 cards in the merged `mesh_hints` catalogue · 21 in `stl_hints` · 2 skills · 3 services · smoke and live tested

## Install

Requirements: Node ≥ 20, DSH `>= 0.2.2-rc.1 < 0.3.0`, **`sim-core/` next to the
bundles** (relative import `../sim-core/...`), an OpenFOAM installation (com or org).
No project checkout is required: generator scripts ship in `mesh-stl/generators/` and STL QA
runs in-process on JS. Python is needed only for the python families
(`trimesh`, `numpy`; `cadquery`/`scipy`/`skimage` for specific ones) and for the parity
test (`tools/qa/stl_qa.py` is the reference, not a dependency).

```json
{ "action": "install_bundle", "target": "/path/to/dsh-mesh-toolkit/mesh-stl" }
{ "action": "install_bundle", "target": "/path/to/dsh-mesh-toolkit/mesh-build" }
```

Keep the three directories as siblings — `sim-core` is a library, not a bundle, so
there is nothing to install for it. The installer adds a `link:` dependency to the
profile and enables the bundle.
After editing `index.js`, `lib/*` or `data/*.json`, reload with disable → enable —
a repeated `enabled: true` reports `changed: false` and does not re-import.

Disable with `set_plugin` `enabled: false`; remove with `remove_bundle` (bundle package name).

Smoke tests without a DSH host (need the project, or `MESH_*_PROJECT_ROOT`):

```bash
node mesh-stl/scripts/smoke.mjs
node mesh-build/scripts/smoke.mjs
```

## OpenFOAM versions

Installations live in `sim-project.json → foam.installations`; each tool accepts
`openfoam: "<id>"` or an absolute `etc/bashrc`, defaulting to `foam.default`.

| Capability | OpenFOAM.com (v2412…v2606) | OpenFOAM.org (v14) |
|---|---|---|
| cfMesh (`cartesianMesh`, `pMesh`, …) | yes | **no** |
| `surfaceFeatureExtract` | yes | stub (rc=0, writes nothing) |
| `surfaceFeatures` + `surfaceFeaturesDict` | no | yes |
| `reconstructParMesh -mergeTol` | yes | no |
| `locationsInMesh` (multi-region snappy) | yes | **no** (single `locationInMesh`) |
| `foamRun` / `foamMultiRun` | no | yes |

The snappy route picks the feature dictionary and the merge flag automatically; `cfmesh`
preflight refuses on org with an actionable message. Same STL and settings gave
`maxNonOrtho` 9.7073° on com2512/com2606 and 25.2146° on org14 with identical 2584 cells —
compare metrics between builds, not only between runs. Matrix: `tools/qa/of_matrix.sh`.

## Configuration

A project is described by **`sim-project.json`** in its root (schema:
`sim-core/schemas/sim-project.schema.json`): `units`, `caseRoots`, `scratch`, `foam`,
`fluent`, `gate {engine, profile, profiles, minVol, script}`,
`geometry {registry, workRoot, scriptRoots}`, `cores`, `physics`. The resolver walks up
to 12 levels from the session cwd; without a profile both plugins still work from the
cwd, and `primitive` needs nothing at all.

Precedence: `sim-project.json` → `config` in `cordis.patch.yml` →
`~/.config/{mesh-stl,mesh-build}/config.json` (override with `MESH_STL_CONFIG` /
`MESH_BUILD_CONFIG`) → `MESH_STL_*` / `MESH_BUILD_*` environment variables.

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `projectRoot` | auto-detect | walk up from the session cwd for `sim-project.json`; without one the tools run on defaults (`project: "defaults"`) |
| `workRoot` | `stl/generated` / `.cache/mesh-build` | project-relative output root |
| `registry` | `stl/registry.csv` | STL passport |
| `caseRoot` | `cases` | mesh-build case lookup root (cwd-relative; `caseRoots: ["./cases"]`) |
| `foam.installations` / `foam.default` | profile | named OpenFOAM builds (`{id: {bashrc}}`); every tool takes `openfoam: "<id>|<bashrc>"` |
| `openfoamBashrc` | auto | explicit `etc/bashrc`; otherwise `foam.default`, `openfoamRoots`, then `/usr/lib/openfoam`, `/opt/openfoam`, `~/openfoam` (newest wins) |
| `openfoamRoots` | `[]` | extra trees, `MESH_*_OPENFOAM_ROOTS` (colon-separated) |
| `python` | `<project>/.venv/bin/python` | interpreter for generators and gmsh |

No machine-specific paths ship in the repository — install targets, project roots and
OpenFOAM locations are placeholders. When the project cannot be found, a tool returns
`configured: false` with the exact setting to provide instead of throwing.

## What you get

**sim-core** — one implementation of everything both plugins share: layered config,
project profile, path resolver with `resolvedFrom`, process runner (`source bashrc` →
`set -u`), `checkMesh -meshQuality` parser, quality gate, artifact passports, knowledge
store. `meshQualityDict` is written with all 13 keys; the verdict comes from the log
text, because `checkMesh` exits 0 even on `Failed N mesh checks`. `foam.js` resolves a
named installation and `withFoam()` binds one to a single tool call.

**mesh-stl** — families `fcc-cell`, `channel-spheres`, `double-layer-burner`,
`packing`, `cad-porous`, plus portable `primitive` (box / sphere / cylinder written in
plain JS, no Python, no project data). `geometry.scriptRoots` keeps generators outside
the project; presets resolve from `@package/...`. `stl_generate` runs the real
generator and QA-verifies every output; `stl_check` cleans and registers.

**mesh-build** — routes `snappy`, `cfmesh`, `gmsh`, `check`; `mesh_build` with
`scaffold: true` writes a runnable snappy case plus `case-manifest.json`, otherwise
builds an existing case; after the gate it writes `mesh-passport.json` (route, cells,
regions, thresholds, sha256/size/mtime of the polyMesh). `mesh_check` reports
`PASS/FAIL/ERROR`, threshold violations and passport freshness, and records the
verdict in `mesh-passport.json`. `mesh_deliver` packages a PASSed case: an OpenFOAM
case with a real `constant/` and `.foam` marker plus `.tar.gz`, an ANSYS/Fluent `.msh`
with `read_mesh.jou` plus `.zip`, and `delivery_<name>.{json,md}`; a stale or missing
passport blocks the run (`force: true` overrides, the delivery gate still runs).

**Skills** — `mesh-stl` and `mesh-build` load on demand and carry the order of work,
hard rules and extension instructions. **Cards** — 32 per catalog: own cards plus the
neighbour's, with shared snappy/plugin cards deduplicated.

## Extending

Rule of thumb: **data first, code second**. Generators, cards, routes and thresholds
are JSON; new tools are plain `defineTool` registrations.

[docs/extending.md](docs/extending.md) — schemas, placeholders, step conditions,
profiles, scaffold options and the reload rule.

## Benchmark

[benchmark/TESTS.md](benchmark/TESTS.md) is the universal regression suite for both
plugins: 10 groups (A–V, L) with exact parameters, analytic references, gate acceptance
and time budgets —

- **A** primitives: cube, sphere, cylinder, box override, STL accuracy;
- **B** channel with 6/28 spheres: snappy, cfMesh, parallel run;
- **C** external flow: sphere refinement study, cube, cylinder, crossing-cylinder block;
- **D** dispersed/multiphase geometry: suspension packing, interface refinement, a
  documented gap for a stratified channel;
- **E** porous media: FCC cell

# mesh-stl — DSH plugin for STL generation

A set of three tools for the `Mesh_3D_pore_scale` project: parametric geometry generation, STL contract
checking and a passport row in `stl/registry.csv`. It runs on the project's real scripts
(`geometry/`) and invents nothing: every metric is computed by its own JS QA (`lib/qa/`), while
`tools/qa/stl_qa.py` remains the parity reference and is available as `engine: "python"`.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Arguments |
|---|---|---|
| `stl_hints` | knowledge cards: the STL contract, cleanup, tessellation, gaps, snappy traps | `query`, `id`, `limit` |
| `stl_generate` | run a generator from the family registry | `family`, `preset`, `name`, `outDir`, `params`, `dryRun` |
| `stl_check` | STL QA + cleanup + passport row | `stl`, `cleanup`, `cleanOut`, `expectVolume`, `expectArea`, `expectBodies`, `maxVolumeErr`, `maxAreaErr`, `register`, `family`, `generator`, `paramsFile`, `fluidOrSolid`, `notes` |


## Description and topics

**Description** (the bundle passport, `package.json` → `description`): STL generation from verified families
(FCC cell, channel with sphere packing, double-layer burner, packings, CadQuery CAD), contract QA
(watertight, winding, mm), cleanup and a passport in `stl/registry.csv`.

**Topics** (`package.json` → `keywords`, for search/marketplace): `stl`, `geometry`, `pore-scale`,
`cadquery`, `trimesh`, `watertight`, `mesh-preparation`, `qa`, `passport`, `generator-presets`.

**For the chat** (what the model actually sees): the tool `description`s in `index.js`, `description` +
`whenToUse` in `lib/skill.js`, the `plugin-mesh-stl` card in `data/hints/plugin.json` (this card's `topics`
match `keywords`). Routing goes by these texts — when you change the tool set, update them.

With no arguments `stl_generate` lists families and presets, `stl_hints` lists the card catalog.

## Installation

The only supported path is the DSH `plugin_manager` tool (it needs user confirmation):

```json
{ "action": "install_bundle", "target": "<absolute path to the repository>/plugins/mesh-stl" }
```

Substitute your own path — DSH accepts only an absolute one (`$(pwd)/plugins/mesh-stl` from the project root).

It adds a `link:` to the plugin directory in the profile and enables the entry in `dsh.profile.bundles`.
The live session re-reads changed code without a DSH restart: on reload the plugin graph is rebuilt,
and ESM modules are unloaded for those files that changed since the previous read (comparison against disk in
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-hmr`). So after an edit: `plugin_manager` → `set_plugin {target:"include:mesh-stl",
enabled:false}`, then `enabled:true`. A bare disable→enable with unchanged files keeps the old
modules in memory — that is not a configuration error.
A check:

```bash
node plugins/mesh-stl/scripts/smoke.mjs        # without DSH: config, cards, catalog, dry-run
node plugins/mesh-stl/scripts/smoke.mjs --full # + a real FCC generation into .cache/mesh-smoke
```

After installation `mesh-stl` appears in the skill catalog, and `stl_hints`, `stl_generate`, `stl_check`
among the tools. If the plugin activates with a schema error, DSH points to the exact parameter path — fix
`index.js`, then repeat `set_plugin` with `"target": "include:mesh-stl"`.

Requirements: Node ≥ 20, DSH `>= 0.2.2-rc.1 < 0.3.0`. The built-in families (`primitive`,
`stratified-channel`, `box-array`) and STL QA work without python and without project data. The python families
(`fcc-cell`, `channel-spheres`, `double-layer-burner`, `blob-foam`, `packing`, `cad-porous`) run
scripts from this package's `generators/` and require `trimesh`, `numpy` and `networkx` (trimesh without a graph
engine fails with `ImportError: no graph engines available!`; for some families — `cadquery`,
`scipy`, `skimage`). Before a run the plugin checks the imports and returns `python-bridge-missing`
with the install command instead of a traceback.

## Configuration

Precedence: the plugin entry's `config` → external JSON → environment variables.

```json
// ~/.config/mesh-stl/config.json   (or $MESH_STL_CONFIG=/path/config.json)
{
  "projectRoot": "/path/to/Mesh_3D_pore_scale",
  "python": "/path/to/Mesh_3D_pore_scale/.venv/bin/python",
  "workRoot": "stl/generated",
  "registry": "stl/registry.csv",
  "timeoutMs": 1800000
}
```

`projectRoot` and `python` can be omitted: the root is searched upwards from the agent's working directory for
`sim-project.json`, and the interpreter defaults to `<projectRoot>/.venv/bin/python`.
`workRoot`/`registry` are paths **relative** to the project root, and without a profile — **relative to the current
directory**; `registry` may be absolute. The passport table is created on demand (it writes the header
itself). If the file cannot be written (read-only directory, a foreign header), QA is still computed: the result
carries `registered: {ok: false, error, row}` and a warning line in `next`, and the verdict is not broken.

Variables: `MESH_STL_PROJECT_ROOT`, `MESH_STL_PYTHON`, `MESH_STL_WORK_ROOT`, `MESH_STL_REGISTRY`,
`MESH_STL_TIMEOUT_MS`, `MESH_STL_CONFIG`, plus `MESH_STL_OPENFOAM_BASHRC` (an explicit `etc/bashrc`) and
`MESH_STL_OPENFOAM_ROOTS` (extra installation directories, colon-separated, in addition to the standard
`/usr/lib/openfoam`, `/opt/openfoam`, `~/openfoam`).

If the project is not found, the tools do not fail; they return `configured: false` and say what to provide.

## Shared core and built-in generators

The mechanics (config, the `sim-project.json` profile, path resolver, process runner, cards, QA) live in
`../sim-core` (package `sim-core`, 0.4.x); `lib/common.js` is a thin facade. The plugin registers the
`simGeometry` service (`hints`/`generate`/`qa`) and contributes its cards to the shared `simHints`.

Three families write STL in plain JS and work **without a project** and without python: `primitive`
(`lib/primitives.js`), `stratified-channel`
(`lib/generators/stratified.js`; two boxes of 12 triangles each) and `box-array`
(`lib/generators/box-array.js`; a lattice of spheres/cylinders plus a container). The shared triangle emitters are
`lib/shapes.js`. QA of every output is the built-in JS (`lib/qa/`).

`primitive` bodies: `box` (`size_mm`), `sphere` (`radius_mm`, `segments`, `rings`), `cylinder`
(`radius_mm`, `height_mm`, `sections`), `cone` (`radius_bottom_mm`, `radius_top_mm` — `0` gives an apex,
`height_mm`), `pipe` (`radius_outer_mm` > `radius_inner_mm`, `height_mm` — a hollow cylinder with annular caps,
which is not convex, so its inner wall is oriented toward the axis). All of them take `center_mm`,
and every body — or each entry of `parts[]` — accepts `translate_mm`, `rotate_deg` (degrees about the global
X, then Y, then Z) and a uniform `scale`. `parts: [{shape: "box", size_mm: [10,10,10]}, {shape: "cylinder",
radius_mm: 2, height_mm: 10, translate_mm: [20,0,0]}]` writes ONE STL with two closed shells, and
`volume_mm3_theory` is the analytic sum (cone: `pi*h*(r1^2+r1*r2+r2^2)/3`, pipe: `pi*h*(R^2-r^2)`).
Presets `cone_r3_apex_h10`, `cone_frustum_r3_r1_h10`, `pipe_r3_r2_h10`, `parts_cube_and_cylinder` are shipped.

`generators.root` (`sim-project.json` → `generators.root`, or `MESH_STL_GENERATORS_ROOT`) selects the
script tree: `package` (by default `generators/` inside this package) or `project`
(the research `geometry/` through `projectScript`/`projectPreset`). Presets live in `generators/presets/<family>/`.
Extra script trees are set in `sim-project.json.geometry.scriptRoots` (absolute paths):
the resolver returns `resolvedFrom`; a project-relative path is looked up in the project first.

## Generator families (`data/generators.json`)

| id | script (`generators.root = package`) | presets |
|---|---|---|
| `fcc-cell` | `generators/pore_cell/gen_fcc_cell.py` | `generators/presets/pore_cell/fcc_cell_d5*.json` |
| `channel-spheres` | `generators/pore_cell/gen_channel_spheres.py` | `generators/presets/pore_cell/channel_spheres_*.json` |
| `double-layer-burner` | `generators/pore_cell/gen_double_layer_burner.py` | `generators/presets/pore_cell/double_layer_burner_*.json` |
| `blob-foam` | `generators/pore_cell/gen_blob_foam.py` | `generators/presets/pore_cell/blob_foam_*.json` |
| `packing` | `generators/packings/gen_packing_table.py` → `gen_packing_stl.py` | `generators/presets/packings/*.json` |
| `cad-porous` | `generators/cad/gen_cq_porous.py` (+ `py_qa.py`) | `generators/presets/cad/*.json` |
| `primitive` | JS `lib/primitives.js` | `data/primitives/*.json` |
| `stratified-channel` | JS `lib/generators/stratified.js` | `generators/presets/stratified/*.json` |
| `box-array` | JS `lib/generators/box-array.js` | `generators/presets/box-array/*.json` |

With `generators.root = "project"` the python families take `projectScript`/`projectPreset` from
the research tree (`geometry/pore_cell/...`), so the old mode is preserved.

Every run: copy/merge `params.json` → generator steps → a log per step in `<outDir>/logs/` →
QA of every declared output (JS by default) → return `{ok, files[{path, qa}], commands, next}`.

## Portable mode (without `sim-project.json`)

`stl_generate`/`stl_check` work in an empty directory: the report carries `project: "defaults"`,
relative paths are resolved from the current directory, the registry is `./stl/registry.csv` (created
automatically), outputs go to `./stl/generated/<family>/`. A read-only registry does not break the verdict
(`registered: {ok:false, error, row}`). The full end-to-end scenario, including meshing and delivery, is in
[`mesh-build/docs/PORTABLE.md`](../mesh-build/docs/PORTABLE.md); card `portable-setup`.

## Knowledge cards (`data/hints/*.json`)

`snappy.json` — meshing traps that affect geometry (minVol, units, patches on domain planes,
interface level, layers, `castellatedBufferLayer`, `symmetry`); `geometry.json` — the STL contract, cleanup,
CadQuery tessellation, the clearance rule, the unsuitability of gmsh tetrahedra, named patches, units.

Card format: `id`, `title`, `topics[]`, `status` (`verified|derived|unverified`), `when`, `statement`,
`recipe[]`, `evidence[]`, `improves[]`. Search is word-based with light stemming; an exact match weighs more.

## Extending (without touching code)

- **Add a family**: an object in `data/generators.json` — `script`, `presets.dir`, `preset.include`
  (a glob, so that other families' presets are not shown), `args` with the placeholders `{paramsFile} {outDir} {json}
  {rawOut} {cleanOut} {solidRawOut} {solidOut} {fluidRawOut} {fluidOut} {fluidPatchesOut} {ballsCsv}
  {contactsCsv} {packingJson}`, `outputs[{path, role, qa}]`, `steps[]` (several steps sharing the same context).
- **Remove a family/route**: delete the entry — the tool stops offering it.
- **Add knowledge**: a JSON card in `data/hints/`; `statement` is a checkable fact, `evidence` — experiment numbers
  and/or verbatim errors.
- After an edit: `node scripts/smoke.mjs` (works without DSH) and a bundle reload —
  `plugin_manager set_plugin {target:"include:mesh-stl", enabled:false}` → `enabled:true`.
  No DSH restart is needed: changed modules are unloaded from the ESM cache on reload.

## Limits

- It does not build meshes (that is `mesh-build`) and does not run solvers.
- It does not silently "fix" parameters: if a generator fails, `failure` is returned with the log tail and the path to the full log.
- Numbers in the cards come from the project journal (`journal/EXPERIMENTS.md`, `journal/DECISIONS.md`), not from memory.

# dsh-mesh-toolkit

[![ci](https://github.com/AstDen/dsh-mesh-toolkit/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/AstDen/dsh-mesh-toolkit/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

> **0.7.4** · packages: mesh-build 0.7.4 · mesh-stl 0.4.1 · sim-core 0.5.1
> host-only plugins distilled from the `Mesh_3D_pore_scale` project. Build a
> watertight STL, turn it into a checked OpenFOAM mesh, then package it as an
> OpenFOAM case plus an ANSYS/Fluent `.msh`. Seven tools, 21–35 searchable knowledge
> cards per catalog, no build step. Meshing routes adapt to OpenFOAM.com **or** OpenFOAM.org.
> Every checked case carries a `handoff.json` (schema `mesh-handoff/1`) for a solver-side workbench,
> and the optional `meshToolkit` service (`apiVersion: 1`) lets one call mesh, gate and deliver.

| Package | Jobs | Tools |
|---|---|---|
| [`sim-core/`](sim-core/) | config layering, `sim-project.json`, path resolver, checkMesh parser, JS quality gate, passports, shared cards | library, no tools |
| [`mesh-stl/`](mesh-stl/) | STL families and portable primitives, in-plugin JS contract QA (python `stl_qa.py` as parity reference), cleanup, passport row | `stl_hints` · `stl_generate` · `stl_check` |
| [`mesh-build/`](mesh-build/) | snappyHexMesh / cfMesh / gmsh route D on any OpenFOAM build, JS quality gate, mesh passport, OF+Fluent delivery | `mesh_hints` · `mesh_build` · `mesh_check` · `mesh_deliver` |

Thin wrappers over the project's real generators and OpenFOAM binaries. No invented
metrics: every number comes from a real run, full logs stay on disk, the tool returns
a compact JSON summary. Plugins talk to each other through Cordis services
(`simHints`, `simGeometry`, `simMesh`), not through each other's files.

## Status

Validated on **OpenFOAM.com v2512**, **v2606** and **OpenFOAM.org v14**, **ParaView 6.2.1**,
**gmsh 4.15.2**, **CadQuery 2.8.0**, Node 24.

**9 tools · 39 cards in the merged `mesh_hints` catalogue · 21 in `stl_hints` · 2 skills · 3 services · smoke and live tested

## Install

Requirements: Node ≥ 20, DSH `>= 0.2.2-rc.1 < 0.3.0`, **`sim-core/` next to the
bundles** (relative import `../sim-core/...`), an OpenFOAM installation (com or org).
No project checkout is required: generator scripts ship in `mesh-stl/generators/` and STL QA
runs in-process on JS. Python is needed only for the python families
(`trimesh`, `numpy`; `cadquery`/`scipy`/`skimage` for specific ones) and for the parity
test (`tools/qa/stl_qa.py` is the reference, not a dependency).

```json
{ "action": "install_bundle", "target": "/path/to/dsh-mesh-toolkit/mesh-stl" }
{ "action": "install_bundle", "target": "/path/to/dsh-mesh-toolkit/mesh-build" }
```

Keep the three directories as siblings — `sim-core` is a library, not a bundle, so
there is nothing to install for it. The installer adds a `link:` dependency to the
profile and enables the bundle.
After editing `index.js`, `lib/*` or `data/*.json`, reload with disable → enable —
a repeated `enabled: true` reports `changed: false` and does not re-import.

Disable with `set_plugin` `enabled: false`; remove with `remove_bundle` (bundle package name).

Smoke tests without a DSH host (need the project, or `MESH_*_PROJECT_ROOT`):

```bash
node mesh-stl/scripts/smoke.mjs
node mesh-build/scripts/smoke.mjs
```

## OpenFOAM versions

Installations live in `sim-project.json → foam.installations`; each tool accepts
`openfoam: "<id>"` or an absolute `etc/bashrc`, defaulting to `foam.default`.

| Capability | OpenFOAM.com (v2412…v2606) | OpenFOAM.org (v14) |
|---|---|---|
| cfMesh (`cartesianMesh`, `pMesh`, …) | yes | **no** |
| `surfaceFeatureExtract` | yes | stub (rc=0, writes nothing) |
| `surfaceFeatures` + `surfaceFeaturesDict` | no | yes |
| `reconstructParMesh -mergeTol` | yes | no |
| `locationsInMesh` (multi-region snappy) | yes | **no** (single `locationInMesh`) |
| `foamRun` / `foamMultiRun` | no | yes |

The snappy route picks the feature dictionary and the merge flag automatically; `cfmesh`
preflight refuses on org with an actionable message. Same STL and settings gave
`maxNonOrtho` 9.7073° on com2512/com2606 and 25.2146° on org14 with identical 2584 cells —
compare metrics between builds, not only between runs. Matrix: `tools/qa/of_matrix.sh`.

## Configuration

A project is described by **`sim-project.json`** in its root (schema:
`sim-core/schemas/sim-project.schema.json`): `units`, `caseRoots`, `scratch`, `foam`,
`fluent`, `gate {engine, profile, profiles, minVol, script}`,
`geometry {registry, workRoot, scriptRoots}`, `cores`, `physics`. The resolver walks up
to 12 levels from the session cwd; without a profile both plugins still work from the
cwd, and `primitive` needs nothing at all.

Precedence: `sim-project.json` → `config` in `cordis.patch.yml` →
`~/.config/{mesh-stl,mesh-build}/config.json` (override with `MESH_STL_CONFIG` /
`MESH_BUILD_CONFIG`) → `MESH_STL_*` / `MESH_BUILD_*` environment variables.

| Setting | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `projectRoot` | auto-detect | walk up from the session cwd for `sim-project.json`; without one the tools run on defaults (`project: "defaults"`) |
| `workRoot` | `stl/generated` / `.cache/mesh-build` | project-relative output root |
| `registry` | `stl/registry.csv` | STL passport |
| `caseRoot` | `cases` | mesh-build case lookup root (cwd-relative; `caseRoots: ["./cases"]`) |
| `foam.installations` / `foam.default` | profile | named OpenFOAM builds (`{id: {bashrc}}`); every tool takes `openfoam: "<id>|<bashrc>"` |
| `openfoamBashrc` | auto | explicit `etc/bashrc`; otherwise `foam.default`, `openfoamRoots`, then `/usr/lib/openfoam`, `/opt/openfoam`, `~/openfoam` (newest wins) |
| `openfoamRoots` | `[]` | extra trees, `MESH_*_OPENFOAM_ROOTS` (colon-separated) |
| `python` | `<project>/.venv/bin/python` | interpreter for generators and gmsh |

No machine-specific paths ship in the repository — install targets, project roots and
OpenFOAM locations are placeholders. When the project cannot be found, a tool returns
`configured: false` with the exact setting to provide instead of throwing.

## What you get

**sim-core** — one implementation of everything both plugins share: layered config,
project profile, path resolver with `resolvedFrom`, process runner (`source bashrc` →
`set -u`), `checkMesh -meshQuality` parser, quality gate, artifact passports, knowledge
store. `meshQualityDict` is written with all 13 keys; the verdict comes from the log
text, because `checkMesh` exits 0 even on `Failed N mesh checks`. `foam.js` resolves a
named installation and `withFoam()` binds one to a single tool call.

**mesh-stl** — families `fcc-cell`, `channel-spheres`, `double-layer-burner`,
`packing`, `cad-porous`, plus portable `primitive` (box / sphere / cylinder written in
plain JS, no Python, no project data). `geometry.scriptRoots` keeps generators outside
the project; presets resolve from `@package/...`. `stl_generate` runs the real
generator and QA-verifies every output; `stl_check` cleans and registers.

**mesh-build** — routes `snappy`, `cfmesh`, `gmsh`, `check`; `mesh_build` with
`scaffold: true` writes a runnable snappy case plus `case-manifest.json`, otherwise
builds an existing case; after the gate it writes `mesh-passport.json` (route, cells,
regions, thresholds, sha256/size/mtime of the polyMesh). `mesh_check` reports
`PASS/FAIL/ERROR`, threshold violations and passport freshness, and records the
verdict in `mesh-passport.json`. `mesh_deliver` packages a PASSed case: an OpenFOAM
case with a real `constant/` and `.foam` marker plus `.tar.gz`, an ANSYS/Fluent `.msh`
with `read_mesh.jou` plus `.zip`, and `delivery_<name>.{json,md}`; a stale or missing
passport blocks the run (`force: true` overrides, the delivery gate still runs).

**Skills** — `mesh-stl` and `mesh-build` load on demand and carry the order of work,
hard rules and extension instructions. **Cards** — 32 per catalog: own cards plus the
neighbour's, with shared snappy/plugin cards deduplicated.

## Extending

Rule of thumb: **data first, code second**. Generators, cards, routes and thresholds
are JSON; new tools are plain `defineTool` registrations.

[docs/extending.md](docs/extending.md) — schemas, placeholders, step conditions,
profiles, scaffold options and the reload rule.

## Benchmark

[benchmark/TESTS.md](benchmark/TESTS.md) is the universal regression suite for both
plugins: 10 groups (A–V, L) with exact parameters, analytic references, gate acceptance
and time budgets —

- **A** primitives: cube, sphere, cylinder, box override, STL accuracy;
- **B** channel with 6/28 spheres: snappy, cfMesh, parallel run;
- **C** external flow: sphere refinement study, cube, cylinder, crossing-cylinder block;
- **D** dispersed/multiphase geometry: suspension packing, interface refinement, a
  documented gap for a stratified channel;
- **E** porous media: FCC cell (baseline 27 424 cells / 41.34°), mono- and
  polydisperse packings;
- **F** hints: query → expected card ids, including the advisory/refusal behaviour;
- **G/H** tool contracts and negative tests; **V** version comparison
  com2512 / com2606 / org14; **L** delivery packaging.

A run writes `benchmark/run-<ts>/{calls.csv,metrics.json,REPORT.md}` and is scored
geometry 20 · mesh 25 · robustness 20 · ergonomics 20 · performance 15.

[benchmark/PROMPT.md](benchmark/PROMPT.md) is the shorter two-task variant (primitives
and packings) for a quick evaluation pass.

## Limits

- No solvers and no Fluent run: the delivery builds the `.msh` and the journal, it does
  not open Fluent. Meshing itself stops at a passing gate.
- The gate is JS (`sim-core/lib/gate.js`); `tools/qa/mesh_gate.sh` is kept only as a
  parity reference and `gate.engine: "script"` escape hatch.
- `mesh-passport.json` records what the gate saw; `mesh_check` compares size+mtime,
  then sha256, and reports `stale` instead of silently trusting an old verdict.
- Patch semantics are not assigned: CAD/STL surfaces become `wall`, so inlet/outlet
  types still need a manual `boundary` edit before a solver run.
- The gmsh route expects a ready OCC script and `.msh`; no gmsh scaffold is generated.
- `minVol` and `minTetQuality` are absolute volumes; pass `minVol` per mesh and record
  it in the run report.
- cfMesh layers over tetrahedra and `polyDualMesh` for CHT were rejected — see the
  `rejected-routes` and `cfmesh-layers-tetra` cards.

## Layout

```
README.md                 this file
benchmark/TESTS.md         universal regression suite (A–V, L)
benchmark/PROMPT.md       shorter two-task evaluation protocol
docs/extending.md         data schemas, routes, thresholds, reload rule
docs/PORTABLE.md          working without sim-project.json
docs/WORKBENCH-CONTRACT.md  mesh-toolkit ↔ openfoam-workbench contract (schemas, roles, loop)
docs/PLAN-workbench-integration.md  analysis of the workbench, adoption methodology, work items
sim-core/                 shared library (not installed as a bundle)
  lib/config.js           layered config + sim-project.json discovery
  lib/project.js          profile normalisation, built-in gate profiles
  lib/paths.js            absolute → cwd → caseRoots → projectRoot resolver
  lib/process.js          source bashrc → set -u, runPython
  lib/hints.js            card store, simHints service
  lib/checkmesh.js        metrics, violations, verdict from log text
  lib/gate.js             full meshQualityDict, .mesh-gate overlay, PASS/FAIL/ERROR
  lib/passport.js         mesh-passport.json, case-manifest.json, freshness
  schemas/*.json          sim-project, mesh-passport, case-manifest, stl-passport
mesh-stl/                 STL plugin
  index.js                3 tools + skill + simGeometry service
  lib/                    facade config, hints, generators, primitives, registry
  data/generators.json    families and presets (incl. primitive)
  data/primitives/*.json  cube / sphere / cylinder presets
  data/hints/*.json       20 cards
  scripts/smoke.mjs
mesh-build/               meshing plugin
  index.js                4 tools + skill + simMesh service
  lib/                    facade config, routes, scaffold, gate adapter, delivery, patches
  data/engine.json        routes and quality profiles
  data/hints/*.json       22 cards
  scripts/smoke.mjs
```

## Provenance and license

Distilled from a pore-scale meshing project (OpenFOAM + ParaView); its thresholds
follow the project's ADRs and the `project` gate profile. No third-party code is
vendored. MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

# DeepSeek Harness (DSH) - WineToken 原生聚合插件

[![DeepSeek Harness](https://img.shields.io/badge/DeepSeek%20Harness-v0.2.2--rc.2-blue)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)
[![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-2.3.0-green.svg)](package.json)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-green.svg)](LICENSE)
[![GitHub Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/AyzRuoshui/dsh-plugin-winetoken)](https://github.com/AyzRuoshui/dsh-plugin-winetoken/releases)

专为 **DeepSeek Harness (dsh) 桌面客户端** 打造的原生官方规范增强插件。仅需配置 WineToken API Key，即可一键将全平台真实上架的精选推理模型（王者荣耀灵宝、GLM-5、Kimi、MiniMax、SenseNova、DeepSeek-V4 等）无缝导入 Harness，并在对话界面底部状态栏原生呈现双账轨（钱包永久余额与周期套餐配额）高精度进度监控与创作工坊。

---

## 核心特性

- **官方标准插件 Bundle 规范**：
  - 严格遵循 Harness 官方 Bundle 规范（`dsh.bundle.patch` 与 `dsh.client`）；
  - 配备完整的国际化元数据（`locale/zh.json`、`locale/en.json`）与纯矢量 SVG 图标；
  - **原生陈列于左侧边栏「插件」中心**，支持在界面中查看详情、启用与管理。
- **现代化 AI 漫剧画布创作工坊 (Comic Canvas Studio)**：
  - **无限视口漫游 (LibTV 对标)**：Ctrl+滚轮/触控板捏合定点缩放 (20%~300%)、滚轮/Shift+滚轮/Space/中键多通道平移、V/H 工具状态机、`Ctrl+0` 一键适应画布总览全部内容；
  - **专业选择集**：橡皮筋框选多选、Shift 加减选、多选批量移动（单次手势单快照）与批量删除、`Ctrl+A` 全选、对齐参考线自动吸附；
  - **万物皆节点 (节点工作流)**：生成图自动作为独立图片节点落画布并连线到源分镜（提示词随节点保存）、通用图片/文本节点、`Tab`/双击空白新建节点菜单、`Ctrl+L` 连线模式与绿色锚点拖出连线、连线可选中删除；
  - **复制三件套**：`Ctrl+D` 复制节点和连线、`Alt+拖动` 克隆节点、`Ctrl+Alt+拖动` 创建副本（保留对外连线）；
  - **组织力**：`Ctrl/Alt+G` 成组 / 解组 / 合并分镜组（组虚线底框 + 成员随动）、`Alt+Shift+F` 整理画布（组波段自动布局 + 适应视图）、`Ctrl+F` 节点搜索（镜号/提示词/台词/角色名/组名定位居中）、AABB 视口虚拟化支撑百卡长画布；
  - **AI 剧本拆镜自动铺图**：粘贴剧本文本一键调用对话模型结构化拆解为分镜卡阵列（含景别/提示词/台词），自动铺上画布；
  - **角色 DNA 锚定**：多角色资产库与参考图绑定，彻底解决跨分镜人物“换脸”与画风漂移问题；
  - **WAL 异步任务队列**：引入 Write-Ahead Log 本地离线任务队列与三级水合保活机制，彻底解决切 Tab 或刷新丢图丢状态问题；
  - **撤销/重做堆栈**：基于命令模式实现 30 步动作栈（覆盖节点/连线/组），支持全局 `Ctrl+Z` / `Ctrl+Shift+Z` / `Ctrl+Y`；
  - **画布快捷键速查面板与五步新手引导**：工具栏「快捷键」弹层四栏速查，交互完全对标 LibTV；
  - **条漫长图自适应导出**：离屏 Canvas 渲染导出高清条漫，台词对白多行自适应折行断句，杜绝溢出重叠。
- **左侧导航栏原生「创作工坊」与 Tool Calling 技能体系**：
  - 无缝接入主导航栏，拥有独立全功能生图与生视频工作空间；
  - **原生大模型工具调用 (Tool Calling)**：大模型在对话中可直接调用工坊生图与视频技能，支持会话级滑动窗口熔断保护与本地垫图自动 Base64 管道；
  - **全链路真实视频生成**：工坊视频模式直连云端网关，支持 MiniMax-H3 与 Grok 视频模型异步长轮询与实时进度展示；
  - **前置余额校验与受控并发**：批量生成前自动校验账户总可用额度，采用受控并发池（Concurrency Limit=2）杜绝瞬时击穿。
- **对话底部状态栏原生资产展示 (双账轨引擎)**：
  - 无缝接入状态栏（`data-composer-dock`），样式与官方风格深度契合；
  - 严格隔离“套餐限时配额”与“钱包永久资产”，30 秒定时静默轮询，点击胶囊可随时手动刷新；
  - 界面遵循零 Emoji 纯矢量极简工业设计，黑白双主题原生自适应。
- **开机模型动态同步与全模态规格推断**：
  - 启动时自动与 WineToken 官方 Manifest 中枢拉齐，映射真实上下文、输出上限与视觉/推理能力；
  - 彻底消除 TDZ 暂存死区风险，移除任意进程误杀逻辑，运行环境平稳可靠。

---

## 安装与使用

### 方式一：客户端界面原生安装 (推荐)
1. 打开 **DeepSeek Harness** 客户端；
2. 点击左侧边栏的 **「插件」** 图标；
3. 点击右上角的 **「+ 添加插件」**，在下拉菜单中选择 **「安装第三方插件」**；
4. 粘贴安装地址：
   - **国内免魔法高速镜像**：
     ```text
     https://ghproxy.net/https://github.com/AyzRuoshui/dsh-plugin-winetoken/archive/refs/tags/v2.3.0.tar.gz
     ```
   - **GitHub 官方直链**：
     ```text
     https://github.com/AyzRuoshui/dsh-plugin-winetoken/archive/refs/tags/v2.3.0.tar.gz
     ```
5. 点击确认完成安全增量安装；首次在底部点击状态胶囊配置 API Key 即可！

### 方式二：本地安全增量安装脚本 (离线或本地源码开发)
在工程根目录下运行安装脚本：
```bash
node scripts/safe_install.cjs
```

---

## 项目结构

```text
dsh-plugin-winetoken/
├── locale/
│   ├── zh.json                 # 官方规范中文插件介绍
│   └── en.json                 # 官方规范英文插件介绍
├── src/
│   ├── index.js                # Host 端插件入口 (生命周期注入 & 资源清理)
│   ├── client.js               # Client 端核心模块 (状态栏胶囊、工坊、AI漫剧画布)
│   ├── credentials.js          # 统一凭据中枢 (跨进程、别名兼容与自动对齐)
│   ├── patch-engine.js         # 纯原生零依赖 Patch 增量合并引擎 (保留注释与用户provider)
│   ├── canvas-storage.js       # 漫剧画布独立持久化存储驱动 (原子双写双备份)
│   ├── canvas-job-queue.js     # WAL 预写日志异步任务队列驱动 (防切Tab丢图)
│   ├── canvas-math.js          # 画布数学计算工具 (贝塞尔曲线、网格磁吸、文本折行)
│   ├── canvas-history.js       # 命令模式 30 步撤销/重做堆栈 (Undo/Redo)
│   ├── tool.js                 # 大模型 Tool Calling 原生技能注入引擎 (带熔断器与尺寸智能对齐)
│   ├── parser.js               # 智能模型元数据解析引擎
│   ├── updater.js              # 安全版本检查器 (只读检查无覆写)
│   ├── history.js              # 本地画廊创作历史库管理
│   └── sync.js                 # Cordis 配置安全合并器 (消除 TDZ 与进程误杀)
├── tests/
│   ├── canvas-math.test.js     # 画布几何计算与长文本折行单元测试
│   ├── canvas-storage.test.js  # 本地工程原子落盘与恢复测试
│   ├── canvas-job-queue.test.js# WAL 异步任务状态机测试
│   ├── circuit-breaker.test.js # 会话级熔断器状态机测试
│   ├── credentials.test.js     # 凭据别名解析与换行符防御测试
│   ├── patch-engine.test.js    # 零依赖增量合并与注释保留测试
│   ├── image-size.test.js      # 图像尺寸 32 倍数智能对齐测试
│   └── sync-security.test.js   # 凭据安全与防误杀单元测试
├── scripts/
│   ├── safe_install.cjs        # 官方标准安全增量合并安装器
│   ├── release.cjs             # 自动化 GitHub Release 发布工具
│   └── publish_to_github.cjs   # 基于 GitHub REST API 的免 Git CLI 发布引擎 (带脱敏审计)
├── cordis.patch.yml            # 官方 Bundle 补丁定义
├── icon.svg                    # 官方规范矢量图标
└── package.json                # 插件元数据与依赖定义 (v2.3.0)
```

---

## 开源许可证

本项目基于 [MIT License](LICENSE) 开源发布。

# Tobs [中文](https://github.com/BotHarness/DeepSeekBot/blob/main/README.md) ｜ **English** [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@botharness/tobs?style=flat-square&color=3d5afe&label=npm)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@botharness/tobs) [![MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-71964a?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/BotHarness/DeepSeekBot/blob/main/LICENSE) [![DeepSeek Harness](https://img.shields.io/badge/built_for-DeepSeek_Harness-b8702f?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) **Tobs: the open-source Grok Bot alternative. A crew of bots, each with its own identity, persona and memory, working together.** [Website](https://tobs.app/en/) · [Video](#video) · [Install](#install) · [Features](#features) · [Releases](#releases) · [vs. DS Bot](#deepseek-bot-projects) · [Community](#community) · [Docs](https://tobs.app/en/docs/overview/)
## Video Tobs in three minutes: a crew of bots with their own identity, persona and memory, working together in a small town. Recorded under the former DeepSeekBot name. Click the poster to play.

Tobs is BotHarness’s MIT-licensed, open-source Grok Bot alternative, running as a plugin in [DeepSeek Harness (DSH)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). Create Bots for research, writing or coding and work with them like colleagues: chat one to one, bring them into a group, hand them tasks. They remember you, do things on schedule, and answer you under their own identity in Slack, Discord, Lark / Feishu, QQ and WeChat. Bots use the model providers and quota you set up in DSH, and the machine running DSH has to stay online for Bots to keep working in the background. Tobs is a different project from the similarly named DS Bot (npm `ds-bot`); see [how they differ](#deepseek-bot-projects). ## Install Tobs was formerly named **DeepSeekBot**. The `deepseekbot` npm package and command remain supported for existing users; new installations use `@botharness/tobs`, with the `tobs` command. Follow the [installation guide](https://tobs.app/en/docs/installation/) for the current verified installation command; install and enable it in DeepSeek Harness, and **Bot mode** appears in the sidebar. No DSH yet? [Get the desktop app](https://www.deepseek.com/en/harness/). For command-line install, version notes and troubleshooting, see the [installation guide](https://tobs.app/en/docs/installation/). ## What you can do with it | You want | How Tobs helps | | ------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **A small AI team of your own** | Create a researcher, a designer, an engineer. Each Bot has a name, a persona and a pixel avatar, and stays the same Bot across conversations. | | **Bots that remember you** | Bots keep your preferences and project context and pick up where they left off. You can read and correct their memory, and sync it to other computers. | | **Several Bots on one job** | Bring Bots into a group chat and @ whoever you need. Hand a bigger task to one Bot to work on separately; it reports back and asks when it needs your call. | | **Bots in the chat apps you use** | Connect Bots to Slack, Discord, Lark / Feishu, QQ and WeChat. @ them in a group or message them directly, and they reply in place under their own identity; in WeChat DMs they can also send and receive files. | | **Things done on time** | Say “send me a log summary every morning at 9” and the Bot sets up the schedule itself, or set one to run every few minutes, hours or days. | | **Help on your computer and browser** | Once you allow it, a Bot can open web pages, click, type and take screenshots, or work on a shared desktop. You watch it live and can pause it any time. | | **Ready-made Bots in one click** | Browse and install Bots other people share in the [Bot Marketplace](https://tobs.app/en/market), share your own, or send a Bot to a friend as a zip. | | **Know what each update brings** | After an update, Bot mode shows what is new; check for and install updates from Settings in one click. | ### Pixel avatars Every Bot gets a pixel avatar made from its name, and while it works the avatar morphs into the tool it is using. Want to make one? Type a name in the [Avatar Studio](https://tobs.app/en/avatar) on our website and download it in high resolution. ## Screenshots

Bot DMs and memory evolution: Mira finds the visitor numbers in her memory; every commit and branch of that memory is on the right.
Group chats: @ three Bots and each replies; Nova reads the first two before answering.

Schedules: one sentence and the Bot sets up the task.
Bot Marketplace: find Bots by topic or keyword and install one as a new colleague (sample data).

Home and Tob: put panels side by side; ask Tob and it reports on all your Bots.
Appearance: themes, colors, a wallpaper library and see-through panels, saved on this device only.
_Screenshots from an isolated local DSH; the conversations are a fictional observatory-exhibition example._ ## Memory you can see Each Bot's memory is a plain Git repository. In the sidebar you can read what it remembers and see which lines changed and when, and edit anything that is wrong. Push it to GitHub to use the same Bot on several computers. See the [memory evolution guide](https://tobs.app/en/docs/channel-sidebar/memory-evolution/). ## Release highlights Full history on the [website changelog](https://tobs.app/en/changelog/). | Version | What's new | | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | **[1.7.0](https://github.com/BotHarness/DeepSeekBot/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md#170---2026-11-12)** | **Call your Bots**, with screen or camera sharing on supported platforms; read and search saved chats on your phone; receive charts and rich documents; improved connection recovery and conversation behavior. The phone app ships separately. | | **[1.6.1](https://github.com/BotHarness/DeepSeekBot/releases/tag/v1.6.1)** (2026-11-02) | **Bot Network**: Bots on computers in the same Tailscale network, under the same Connect account, or on a LAN both sides approve can find and message each other; long conversations and chat switching are much smoother, and Bot avatars are now static images; the composer's model button opens model settings directly; bundled cloudflared security update. Upgrading migrates local data, so 1.6.0 cannot open it afterwards. | | **[1.6.0](https://github.com/BotHarness/DeepSeekBot/releases/tag/v1.6.0)** (2026-10-29) | A **Simple layout mode** for Bot mode; the **Bot Marketplace** gains uploads, daily picks and a review by Tob before install; see an Assignment's work by Orchestrator round; QQ private messages and Bot-to-Bot mentions in Lark and Discord; many desktop and mobile fixes. | | **[1.5.2](https://github.com/BotHarness/DeepSeekBot/releases/tag/v1.5.2)** (2026-10-25) | **Native desktop zoom is enabled by default**, without extra setup; fixes improve Windows/macOS Computer component reuse and setup errors. | | **[1.5.1](https://github.com/BotHarness/DeepSeekBot/releases/tag/v1.5.1)** (2026-10-25) | **Tobs ships as `@botharness/tobs`**, keeping the supported `deepseekbot` entry; Bots use one delivery path for Channels and external chats; **background task results** can wake an idle Bot and report back; fixes restore installed CLI startup and the return-to-latest-message button. | | **[1.5.0](https://github.com/BotHarness/DeepSeekBot/releases/tag/v1.5.0)** (2026-10-22) | **Tobs Connect** pairs a phone through your account without Tailscale; **Storage** clears old media and messages; the Bot Marketplace becomes a panel; plugins update from Bot settings; Bot mode is fast again on long conversations; the VRM companion installs on its own. | | **[1.4.1](https://github.com/BotHarness/DeepSeekBot/releases/tag/v1.4.1)** (2026-10-20) | A five-step intro from Tob the first time you enter Bot mode; Bot mode gets its own **themes, see-through panels and a wallpaper library**; `/compact` and Idle Compaction keep long conversations fast; quick search jumps to any setting; Memory previews images and Markdown; the mobile Beta adds notification switches. | | **[1.4.0](https://github.com/BotHarness/DeepSeekBot/releases/tag/v1.4.0)** (2026-10-19) | **Tob** on Home manages Bots, models and groups through chat; the desktop becomes a drag-and-drop **panel workspace** that remembers each Channel's layout; a reviewer model can handle approvals; pair a phone; the CLI covers almost everything the UI does. Supports DSH 0.2.0-rc.2 through 0.2.x. | | **[1.3.1](https://github.com/BotHarness/DeepSeekBot/releases/tag/v1.3.1)** (2026-10-14) | Installing `deepseekbot` from the Plugins page takes one step again, with no build approval; needs DSH 0.2.0-rc.2. The `deepseekbot` CLI can configure a Host, drive a Bot's Browser and Computer, and manage IM apps; the Browser panel updates live. | | **[1.3.0](https://github.com/BotHarness/DeepSeekBot/releases/tag/v1.3.0)** (2026-10-14) | One design system across Bot mode, with Channel settings in a dialog; the Orchestrator tidies its own inbox and tasks; Bots use your secrets for CLI tools and **MCP** servers with your approval, and set up MCP from one sentence; **export** multi-selected messages; Bot colors, more pixel species and hand-drawn parts; restore memory to any version. Needs DSH 0.2.0 or later. | | **[1.2.1](https://github.com/BotHarness/DeepSeekBot/releases/tag/v1.2.1)** (2026-10-12) | Fixes installs failing on some DSH versions; group avatars show a grid of member avatars; audio and file attachments play and download in place. | | **[1.2.0](https://github.com/BotHarness/DeepSeekBot/blob/v1.2.0/CHANGELOG.md#120---2026-10-08)** (2026-10-08) | Pixel **Window Companions** you can pin on your desktop; bind one app to message Bots in Lark, Slack, Discord and WeChat; **import and export** Bots as zip files; Bot profiles with a banner and bio. | | **1.1.0** (2026-10-06) | **Schedules**; every conversation carries the Bot's persona and core memory; **one-click update** in Settings; WeChat voice-to-text and images. | | **1.0.1** (2026-10-05) | First stable release: PersonaBots with their own identity, Git memory, group chats, delegated tasks, pixel avatars, IM connections and the first **Bot Marketplace**. | ## Tobs and DS Bot (ds-bot): two projects, different focus The names are close, but these are two independent open-source projects. Both run on DeepSeek Harness (DSH), and neither is an official DeepSeek product. - **Tobs**, this repository, by BotHarness, makes each Bot a long-lived colleague that **works beyond the DSH window**: Git memory you can review, the Bot's own Lark / Slack / Discord / WeChat identity, schedules, delegated Assignments and a Bot Marketplace. - **DS Bot**, [Fei2411/DeepSeek-Bot](https://github.com/Fei2411/DeepSeek-Bot) (npm `ds-bot`, also written DeepSeek Bot in its README), **turns DSH itself into a bot chat app**: a main Bot, Chief, sets up your team through conversation, a group admin answers first to keep token use down, and a Usage page shows tokens by time, Bot and model. | | Tobs | DS Bot (ds-bot) | | ------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Repository | [BotHarness/DeepSeekBot](https://github.com/BotHarness/DeepSeekBot) | [Fei2411/DeepSeek-Bot](https://github.com/Fei2411/DeepSeek-Bot) | | Package | npm [`@botharness/tobs`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@botharness/tobs) | npm [`ds-bot`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/ds-bot) | | License | MIT | Apache-2.0 | | Memory | One Git working tree per Bot: files, commits and diffs; push to GitHub to share it across machines | Markdown memory reviewed after each turn; personal and team levels | | Several Bots | @ whoever you need in a Group; Assignments delegate separate tasks with their own reports | A main Bot manages the team; a group admin answers by default and calls in other Bots | | Beyond DSH | Bots join Lark / Feishu, Slack, Discord and WeChat under their own identity | GitHub connector | | Also | Schedules, Bot Marketplace, Bot import and export, pixel avatars | Schedules, Usage page | **Which one?** If you want Bots to work in your IM under their own identity, or to review and sync memory with Git, try Tobs. If you want a main Bot to walk you through building a team inside DSH and keep an eye on token use, try DS Bot. Both are open source, so read both codebases: [Tobs](https://github.com/BotHarness/DeepSeekBot) · [DS Bot](https://github.com/Fei2411/DeepSeek-Bot). For a longer comparison, see [the article on our website](https://tobs.app/en/blog/deepseekbot-vs-ds-bot/). ## FAQ ### Which DeepSeek Bot project is this? This is **Tobs by BotHarness**: npm package [`@botharness/tobs`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@botharness/tobs), website [tobs.app](https://tobs.app/en/). DS Bot uses `ds-bot` and is a separate project, not a short name or an older version of this one. See [how the two differ](#deepseek-bot-projects). ### Does Tobs require DeepSeek models? No. It uses the providers configured in DSH; availability depends on API support, model settings and credentials. Memory and chat history stay on your host, while calls to a remote model send relevant context to the provider you chose. ## For developers To run from source or contribute, you need Node ≥22 and pnpm. ```bash git clone https://github.com/BotHarness/DeepSeekBot.git BotHarness cd BotHarness pnpm install && pnpm build node scripts/dev-instance.mjs --home /tmp/botharness-demo --port 31967 ``` More in the [local instance guide](docs/client-bridge.md) · [contributing guide](CONTRIBUTING.md) · [architecture](docs/architecture/botharness-architecture.md) · [decisions](docs/decisions/) · [agent guidelines](AGENTS.md) · [Release Ledger](CHANGELOG.md) · [DSH docs](https://deepseek-harness.github.io/deepseek-harness/). For real IM tests, the [shared QA App wizard](docs/agents/im-test-apps.md) configures independent Lark, Slack and Discord QA1/QA2/QA3 slots. For example, run `node scripts/dev-im-test-apps.mjs setup discord` to enter the Token privately; confirm the current exclusive window before each receiver start. ## Community Questions, ideas and the Bots you build are all welcome. | Come say hello | Build something together | | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | [](https://discord.gg/aEB2Ayhu7B) | [Join the Tobs server](https://discord.gg/aEB2Ayhu7B) to ask questions and share your crew. | | | Search for group **1125565676** in QQ. | | [](https://github.com/BotHarness/DeepSeekBot/discussions) | [Questions, ideas and things you have made](https://github.com/BotHarness/DeepSeekBot/discussions) · [Welcome thread](https://github.com/BotHarness/DeepSeekBot/discussions/1397). | | [](CONTRIBUTING.md) | [Contribution guide](CONTRIBUTING.md) · [First contribution](https://github.com/BotHarness/DeepSeekBot/discussions/1398). Docs, tests and answers all help; use [Issues](https://github.com/BotHarness/DeepSeekBot/issues/new/choose) for confirmed bugs and implementation tasks. | | | We are on Product Hunt. Take a look and share Tobs with a friend. |

# Tobs **中文** ｜ [English](https://github.com/BotHarness/DeepSeekBot/blob/main/README.en.md) [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@botharness/tobs?style=flat-square&color=3d5afe&label=npm)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@botharness/tobs) [![MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-71964a?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/BotHarness/DeepSeekBot/blob/main/LICENSE) [![DeepSeek Harness](https://img.shields.io/badge/built_for-DeepSeek_Harness-b8702f?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) **Tobs（托布）：开源的 GrokBot 平替。一组有各自身份、人格和记忆的 bots，一起做事。** [官网](https://tobs.app) · [宣传片](#video) · [安装](#install) · [能力](#features) · [版本亮点](#releases) · [与 DS Bot 的区别](#deepseek-bot-projects) · [社区](#community) · [文档](https://tobs.app/docs/overview/) 赞助商    ·  𝕏 eric_0721 @XXXX540515 创始人
## 宣传片 3 分钟看懂 Tobs：一组有身份、人格和记忆的 bots，在小镇里一起做事。视频录制时仍使用旧名 DeepSeekBot；点击封面即可播放。

Tobs（托布）是 BotHarness 开发的 MIT 开源 GrokBot 平替，作为插件运行在 [DeepSeek Harness（DSH）](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)里。你可以创建几个分别负责研究、写作或写代码的 Bot，像和同事一样私聊、拉群、派活；它们记得你，会按时做事，还能在 Slack、Discord、飞书 / Lark、QQ 和微信里以自己的身份回你消息。 模型用你在 DSH 里配置的服务商和额度；Bot 需要在后台持续工作时，运行 DSH 的电脑要保持在线。它和名字很像的 DS Bot（npm `ds-bot`）是两个独立项目，区别见[下文](#deepseek-bot-projects)。 ## 安装 Tobs（托布）原名 **DeepSeekBot**。已有用户仍可使用 `deepseekbot` npm 包和命令；新用户请安装 `@botharness/tobs`，使用 `tobs` 命令。 按[安装指南](https://tobs.app/docs/installation/)复制当前已验证的安装命令，在 DeepSeek Harness 桌面端安装并启用，侧栏就会出现「Bot 模式」。还没装 DSH？先[下载桌面端](https://www.deepseek.com/en/harness/)。 命令行安装、版本说明和常见问题见[官网安装指南](https://tobs.app/docs/installation/)。 ## 能用它做什么 | 你想要 | Tobs 怎么帮你 | | -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **一支自己的 AI 小团队** | 创建研究员、设计师、工程师等 Bot，每个都有名字、人格和像素头像，换个对话也还是同一个它。 | | **让 Bot 记住你** | Bot 会记下你的偏好和项目背景，下次直接接着干；记忆随时能翻看、纠正，也能同步到别的电脑。 | | **多个 Bot 一起干活** | 把 Bot 拉进群聊，需要谁就 @ 谁；大一点的任务可以交给 Bot 单独去做，做完交回报告，需要你拍板时会提醒你。 | | **在常用的聊天软件里找它** | 把 Bot 接入 Slack、Discord、飞书 / Lark、QQ 和微信，在群里 @ 它或私聊，它就在原处用自己的身份回复；微信私聊里还能收发文件。 | | **定时做事** | 说一句「每天早上 9 点给我发日志摘要」，Bot 就自己建好定时任务；也可以手动设置每隔几分钟、几小时或每天执行。 | | **帮你操作电脑和浏览器** | 授权后，Bot 可以打开网页、点击、输入、截图，或操作一台共享桌面；你能实时看着它做，随时暂停。 | | **一键装别人做好的 Bot** | 在 [Bot 市场](https://tobs.app/market)浏览、安装别人分享的 Bot，也能把自己的 Bot 分享出去，或打包成 zip 发给朋友。 | | **知道每次更新了什么** | 升级后会告诉你这一版新增了什么；在设置里就能检查并一键更新。 | ### 像素头像 每个 Bot 都有一张由名字生成的像素头像，工作时还会变成它正在用的工具。想自己捏一个？到[官网头像工坊](https://tobs.app/avatar)输入名字试试，还能下载高清头像。 ## 截图

Bot 私聊与记忆演化：Mira 从记忆里找出访客统计；右侧能看到它记忆的每次提交和分支。
群聊协作：@ 三个 Bot，它们各自回复，Nova 读完前两位再接话。

定时任务：一句话让 Bot 自己建任务。
Bot 市场：按话题和关键词找 Bot，点「安装」就多一位同事（图中为示例数据）。

首页与托布：面板可以并排摆放；问托布一句，它就汇报所有 Bot 的状态。
界面设置：主题、配色、壁纸库和半透明面板，只保存在这台设备上。
_截图来自隔离的本地 DSH，对话是虚构的天文台展览示例。_ ## 看得见的记忆 每个 Bot 的记忆就是一个普通的 Git 仓库。你可以在侧栏翻看它记了什么、哪天改了哪几行，觉得不对就直接改；推到 GitHub，就能在几台电脑之间共用同一个 Bot。详见[记忆演化指南](https://tobs.app/docs/channel-sidebar/memory-evolution/)。 ##
