产品意图是“自动正确管理”，所以这套机制**默认开启**，用户只能显式关闭、不需要开启。它把「模型坏了」「账号坏了」「这个路由自带池，别插手」三种完全不同的故障分开记账：旧实现只有一个 `isHealthy = !cooldown`，把三者混成一团，且冷却中的账号永远收不到能证明它恢复的那次请求，恢复只能靠时间到点。 | 层 | 模块 | 负责什么 | 判定粒度 | |---|---|---|---| | L1 路由健康 | `lib/availability.js` | 模型/端点是否可用、是否免费 | 精确 `(provider, modelId)` 元组，绝不按 provider 或裸 modelId 合并 | | L2 账号健康 | `lib/account-health.js` | 凭据/额度是否可用、冷却与半开恢复 | `accountId` | | L2a 拓扑 | `lib/provider-topology.js` | 这个路由是不是自带账号池（是就别再包一层） | `provider`（仅作证据标签，不参与分类） | | L7 接线 | `lib/health-setup.js` | 默认开启、opt-out、注册表共享 | —— | | 探测 | `lib/probe.js` | 用一次真实极小请求替代“按模型名猜免费/付费” | `(provider, modelId)` | 三个注册表是**同一个对象引用**：适配器写入的就是设置页首屏读取的，没有第二份镜像。 ### L1 —— 故障分类的关键纠偏 `classifyFailure()` 按 P0→P4 顺序判定，**请求形状问题绝不连累模型健康**： | 优先级 | 类别 | 影响模型健康 | 例子 | |---|---|---|---| | P0 | `SESSION_HEADER` / `PARAM_COMPAT` | 否 | 缺 session 头、`max_completion_tokens` 不支持、`developer` role | | P1 | `RENAMED` / `OFFLINE` | 是 | 404/UNKNOWN_MODEL，配合上游 id 列表判定重命名还是下线 | | P2 | `QUOTA` / `RATE_LIMIT` / `AUTH` | 否 | 402、429、401/403 —— 这是账号层的问题 | | P3 | `SERVER_JITTER` | 连续 3 次才降级 | 5xx、timeout、stream closed | | P4 | `UNKNOWN` | 否 | 无特征指纹的裸 400 | **这是设计里最重要的一条纠偏**：旧实现把所有 4xx 都塞进 `SERVER` 粗桶，于是一个参数不兼容的请求会把一个好模型打成不可用。现在裸 400 落 `UNKNOWN`，`max_completion_tokens` 这类消息落 `PARAM_COMPAT`，两者都不动模型健康。 状态机：`UNKNOWN → HEALTHY`（任意一次成功）；`OFFLINE` 连续 3 次 → `DEPRECATED`；`SERVER_JITTER` 连续 3 次 → `DEGRADED`。**双源零样本一定是 `UNKNOWN` 且 confidence 0，绝不判成“不可用”**。`DEPRECATED`/`DEGRADED` 也不从候选池删除，只是排到后面。 `updateHealth()` 是纯函数：返回新记录、不改入参；虚拟路由副本（如 `smart` 自身）**永不写健康**。 ### L1 —— 免费/付费的证据等级 不靠模型名猜。**用户口径「名字带 free 或者倍率为 0 的可以默认认为免费」已实现为弱信号 / 用户声明默认值（free-signal-v1，未实测）**：名字含 `free`、`priceMultiplier=0`（或 `costModel=free` / `priceTier=free`）即「默认免费（未实测）」：只用于候选收录 / 筛选 / 排序代理与显示「可能免费（未实测）」，等级为 `weak` / `declared`，**不写 L1 billingTier=FREE**；可被真实付费证据（probe `metered`、账本正成本、付费 billingSource、真实正价）推翻。`probeVerdict=unknown` 不阻断弱信号；估算零价（`estimated:true`）不是证据；只有有限数值 `0` 算倍率零。真凭实据的强度：上游 `billingSource`/`cost>0`（高，0.95）> 自己的付费样本（高）> 账本里 20 条以上 cost=0 样本（中，0.7）。只有价格标记、没有任何真实样本时结论是 `UNKNOWN`，不是 `free`。**重命名会强制清零计费证据**：旧价格不能顺延给新 id，必须重新确认，否则“省钱”就是假的。设置页账号行的「价格倍率」可直接修改（留空 / 非法值按 1，`0` = 声明免费）；当前部分路由 probe 多为 `unknown` 的根因尚在验证，不据此宣称任何模型一定免费。免费标签分实测 / 声明 / 未实测三档；实测档按来源显示「已确认免费·价格表 / ·探测 / ·账单」后缀，且按 `(provider, modelId)` 元组取证据（同名模型不跨 provider 串标）；账号倍率 0 属声明级，可被实测付费证据推翻。 ### L2 —— 半开恢复，而不是时间到点自动复活 四个状态与排序权重： | 状态 | 权重 | 含义 | |---|---|---| | `ACTIVE` | 1.0 | 最近一次真实请求成功 | | `UNKNOWN` | 0.8 | 还没有证据 | | `HALF_OPEN` | 0.5 | 冷却到期，**允许一次**真实用户请求来证明自己 | | `COOLING` | 0 | 冷却中，不参与排序 | 冷却到期只会变成 `HALF_OPEN`，永远不会直接 `ACTIVE`；没有真实流量就一直停在 `HALF_OPEN`（**没有证据就没有恢复**）。每次真实请求消耗一个半开许可，结果是成功才回到 `ACTIVE` 并清零连击，失败则继续冷却。全程不需要探测请求。 基础冷却与连击退避（`base × 2^(streak-1)`，上限 24h）：配额 30min、鉴权 24h、限流 1min、抖动 5s。**第一次失败用基础值**，不是翻倍值。 失败分层：`SESSION_HEADER`/`PARAM_COMPAT`（请求构造问题）、`RENAMED`/`OFFLINE`（模型层问题）都**不冷却账号**——“谁的问题谁负责”。`UNKNOWN` 只加样本不惩罚。 ### L2a —— 自带账号池的路由不要重复包一层 有些插件对外是一条路由、内部已经轮换多个账号。再给它套一层账号池，两个池会互相打架。所以先分拓扑，再决定要不要建账号层： | 证据 | 优先级 | 判定 | |---|---|---| | `provider.aggregatesAccounts === true/false` | P0 | 直接采信声明 | | 同一 provider+model 观测到 >1 个不同 `account_id` | P1 | 自带池 | | 声明里有 `accounts`/`regions` 数组或 `pool` 能力 | P1 | 自带池 | | 无任何结构化证据 | P2 | `UNKNOWN`（保守按 direct 处理，但标记未确认） | **硬规则：没有 provider 名字白/黑名单**，分类只能来自结构化证据，`provider` 字符串只用于挂证据与告警。判定为自带池时不建账号层，但**不会静默丢掉**用户配置的 account —— 产生 `AGGREGATOR_ACCOUNTS_IGNORED` 告警交由首屏展示。用户可用 `forceAccountLayer: true` 显式覆盖，这是可逆的显式选择，不是产品默认。 ### 探测 —— 一次 1 token，绝不挡人 客户端拿不到 `stream`（只有 Host 有），所以探测在 Host 侧：每个 `(provider, model)` 发**一次 max_tokens=1** 的请求，读 `usage.cost`/`billingSource` 得出 `free`/`metered`/`unknown`。结论写入 L1 并带正确的置信度；缓存 7 天，单次调用最多 3 个真实探测，超出返回诚实的 `unknown`（附身份，不隐藏）。`unknown` **永不阻断**——“不能挡”这条规则优先于任何猜测。 ### 冷启动水合 —— 重放磁盘上已经证明过的证据（1.2.0） `buildHealthDeps()` 交出的注册表是**空**的，于是 1.2.0 以前每次重载/重启插件，L1 的路由判决（`HEALTHY` / `DEGRADED` / `DEPRECATED`、免费还是付费的计费置信度）与 L2 的账号状态（冷却、连击、样本）全部清零 —— 而这些证据早已被真实流量证明过、就躺在 `cost.jsonl` 里，连 `rebuildFromLedger()` 都没有任何调用方。 现在激活时由 `lib/health-persistence.js` **纯读重放**一次： - **L1 路由层** —— `cost.jsonl` 逐行走 `updateHealth()`，和实时路径、探测共用同一个分类入口（不另写第二套判定），键保持 `(provider, modelId)` 元组粒度，绝不按 provider 或裸 modelId 合并；`probe-cache.jsonl` 里记录的探测结论（`free` / `metered` / `unknown`）也回灌进 L1，同一 `(provider, model)` 只取最新一条，`unknown` 保持诚实样本、不硬判成免费。 - **L2 账号层** —— 同一批行交给 `rebuildFromLedger()` 重建冷却/连击/样本，结果**合并进适配器持有的那个注册表对象**，不是造一份新注册表：首屏读到的就是它。 - **上界 = 4 MiB 尾部字节窗 + 5000 行**（`DEFAULT_HYDRATION_BOUNDS`）。理由：最新几行才代表当前结论；两层本来就有样本上限（L1 滑窗 200、L2 按连击封顶），L1 的计费置信度 20 条免费样本即饱和，重放更老的行不会改变任何判决，只会增加启动耗时。字节窗从行中间开始的那半行会被丢掉，行窗超限时只保留最新 `maxLines` 行。**这两个是常量，没有暴露成用户配置**（见 §十一）。 - **只读 + 容错**：只 `open(file, 'r')` —— 不 mkdir、不 append、不改写。文件缺失（首次运行）、目录不存在、半行（进程被杀在 append 中途）、损坏行、非对象行一律不抛错：坏账本绝不能挡住插件激活。被跳过的行数与原因（`malformed` / `no-key` / `newer-live`）都进 info 汇总。 - **不覆盖更新的实时证据**：水合是 `ctx.effect` 里的 fire-and-forget（`apply()` 是同步的，激活不等磁盘），真实请求可能先落地。每行重放前都比对注册表已有记录的时间戳/`updatedAt`，已经有更新证据就跳过（`newer-live`）；时间戳缺失或非法的行按 0 处理，因此必输给任何实时记录。 - **`health=false` 时不水合**：显式关闭（`health:false` / `health.enabled:false` / `ranking.health.enabled:false`）时 `buildHealthDeps()` 返回 `undefined`，水合返回 `{hydrated:false, reason:'health-disabled'}`，**连文件都不打开**，legacy 路径逐字节不变。 - **一行 info 汇总**，可用来核对实际重放了什么（实际是一条单行，下面为便于阅读折了行）： ``` smart health hydrate: cost.jsonl rows=224 replayed(L1)=224 skipped(L1)=0 (malformed=0 no-key=0 newer-live=0) L2 accounts=3 (newer-live=0 no-account=0) | probe-cache.jsonl rows=3 replayed=1 skipped=0 (malformed=0 duplicate=2 newer-live=0) | total skipped rows=0 | truncated lines=0+0 bytes=0+0 | bounds maxBytes=4194304 maxLines=5000 ``` 这是本机 2026-11-25 对真实账本的一次只读重放：224 行只落到 **4** 个 `(provider, modelId)` 键 —— 行数不等于路由数，L1 是按元组归集的；`probe-cache.jsonl` 的 3 行里 2 行同键被 `duplicate` 计数、只回灌最新 1 条。 ### 关闭方式 `health` 与 `ranking.health` 都是 volatile，配置页可改、无需重启）。默认启用、中立等权：完全没有用户 `ranking` 配置时由 `index.js` 注入 `DEFAULT_RANKING_CONFIG.routing`（`enabled:true` / `balanced` / 四因子 .25）；用户显式写了 `ranking.routing` 时以其为准，`null` 或 `enabled !== true` 时该代码路径完全不运行、逐字节回 legacy。字段格式： ```json { "ranking": { "enabled": false, "strategy": "balanced", "routing": { "enabled": true, "strategy": "balanced", "tierPolicy": "auto", "weights": { "cost": 0.25, "speed": 0.25, "tier": 0.25, "load": 0.25 }, "positionOverrides": { "vendor/model": { "tags": ["reasoning", "longctx"] } }, "tierLimit": 2, "longContextTokens": 200000, "dynamicAuto": [] } } } ``` - `enabled` —— 必须为 `true` 才激活；否则逐字节走 legacy。 - `strategy` —— 8 种预设之一：`balanced` / `cost-first` / `speed-first` / `reasoning-first` / `longctx-first` / `vision-first` / `legacy` / `custom`；`balanced` 是中立默认，省钱（cost-first）是显式选择。 - `tierPolicy` —— 层一强制层（`auto` 不强制；`reasoning-first` / `longctx-first` / `vision-first` 会强制优先选对应位置）。 - `weights` —— 层二账号评分权重，自定义时归一化；routing 启用时会覆盖 ranking 的权重。 - `positionOverrides` —— 手动指定某模型的位置标签（键用 `provider/model` 或 `model`）。**两种形态都受支持**：上面示例的对象形态 `{ "vendor/model": { "tags": ["reasoning"] } }`（**主推**，与 `registry/position-overrides.user.yaml` 里的 `overrides` 完全同形，方便同一份东西在文件与 cordis 配置之间搬），以及数组形态 `{ "vendor/model": ["reasoning"] }`。两种形态都先做小写 / 去空格 / 白名单过滤，再与 catalog 自动推导出的能力标签**保守合并**（合并，不是替换）。**可感知的行为变化**：1.2.0 之前实现只读 `.tags`，于是 README 自己写的数组形态是**静默无效**的 —— 你照文档配了 `positionOverrides`，`selectTiers` 依旧报 `no tier matches ... relaxing`，且没有任何提示；现在数组形态同样生效，两种写法等价。 - `tierLimit` —— 最多选几个候选层（默认 2）。**语义**：非有限值（`NaN`）、`-1`、`0` 一律回落到默认 2（以前 `-1` 会静默少一层、`0` 会匹配上了也一层都不选，直接和「层一永不阻断请求」的契约打架）；小数向下取整（`2.9 → 2`）；`1` / `2` 正常切片。 - `longContextTokens` —— 长上下文判定阈值（默认 200000；tokens 用 chars/4 估算，仅用于选路、不用于计费）。 - `dynamicAuto` —— 动态 auto 链；只在用户没有配置该 outer model 与 `*` 时生效，显式配置始终优先（向后兼容）。 ### 位置标签：自动推导 vs 手填 `derivePosition()` 从模型 catalog 元数据自动推导： - `reasoning === true` → `reasoning` - `contextWindow >= 200000` → `longctx` - `input` 含 `image` → `vision` - `tool !== false` → `tool`（聊天模型默认具备，保守策略避免误杀） - 所有模型都带 `general` 自动结果总是保守、不会因缺元数据而失败。手填（`positionOverrides`，对象形态 `{tags:[...]}` 与数组形态 `[...]` 都收，见上）走的是**合并**而不是替换：手填标签经小写/去空格/白名单过滤后并入 catalog 自动推导出的能力标签，来源标记为 `auto` / `user` / `mixed`。合并是有意的——早期版本用替换，结果给一个免费模型打上 `thrifty` 就把它的 `vision` 冲掉了，能力过滤静默失效。 `thrifty` 与 `swift` **永远无法自动推导**：它们描述的是「便宜」和「快」，catalog 里没有这两个字段，只能靠 `positionOverrides` 手填（`registry/position-overrides.user.yaml` 就是为此存在的）。手填适合 catalog 元数据缺失或不准确时纠正位置。 ### relax 诊断 —— 从「一句话」到「照做就行」（1.2.0） 层一没有候选匹配时不阻断请求：所有可用路由原样放行（relax）。这条规则没变，变的是**告警内容**。以前只报任务类型（`smart routing: no tier matches task "reasoning"; relaxing to all available routes`），你自己得去猜为什么、该改哪里；现在首行**字面保持不变**（`grep 'relaxing to all available routes'` 的老做法继续有效，诊断是紧跟其后的续行），续行把整件事说清楚。 本机直接调用 `selectTiers()` 的实测输出（两个假想路由都不带 `reasoning`）： ``` smart routing: no tier matches task "reasoning"; relaxing to all available routes task: kind="reasoning" signals=[hard-tokens] needed position tag(s): "reasoning" — no candidate route carries "reasoning" candidate routes (2) and the position tags they do carry: - vendor/cheap-flash: tool, general - vendor/big-flash: tool, general, longctx why "reasoning" is missing everywhere: auto-derived only when the model catalog reports reasoning:true fix — declare the tag for a model you actually have (both shapes below work, copy either one): "ranking": {"routing":{"positionOverrides":{"vendor/cheap-flash/":["reasoning"]}}} registry form: {"overrides":{"vendor/cheap-flash/":{"tags":["reasoning"]}}} key = "vendor/cheap-flash/" (replace with a model served by route "vendor/cheap-flash"); a bare model id also works note: tierPolicy only reorders which tier is tried first; it cannot invent a tag that no route carries relax outcome: all 2 route(s) stay available; the request is NOT blocked ``` 诊断固定给出五件事：缺的是哪个位置标签；每个候选路由**实际**带哪些标签（超过 8 个路由会截断并注明「还有 N 个」，不刷屏）；这个标签为什么自动推导不出来（每种标签一条原因，例如 `longctx` 只在 `contextWindow >= longContextTokens` 时自动出现，调大阈值会让更多请求掉进这个坑）；**可复制**的修法（cordis 配置形态与 registry 形态各一份，键用候选里第一个真实路由）；以及 `tierPolicy` `account_id`（服务该尝试的池账号；未配置池时为 `hop:provider/model`）和诊断字段：`cache_read_tokens`、`cache_write_tokens`、`usage_complete`、`price_known`、`request_id`、`seq`。 **延迟度量字段（缺数据时整段不写，不留 0 或 null）**：`started_at` / scripts/query-cost.mjs # 单个模型：美元花费及占全部记录花费的比例 node scripts/query-cost.mjs --model kimi-k3 # 按外层模型 / provider / 账号 / 时间过滤 node scripts/query-cost.mjs --outer auto node scripts/query-cost.mjs --provider opencode-go node scripts/query-cost.mjs --account acctA node scripts/query-cost.mjs --by-account # 按 account_id 汇总花费 node scripts/query-cost.mjs --since 2026-11-23 ``` **报表结构（1.2.0 起）**：前两段（花费汇总 + 分组花费表）**逐字节不变**，老用法不受影响；其后追加两段： - **failure rate（按分组）** —— 该组 `failed / calls`。只有真的写了 `failure_code` 的行算失败；`failure_code` 缺失、`null` 或空串算成功（不会把「没记失败码」误读成失败）。 - **latency（按分组）** —— `ttft ms` 均值、`p50 ms`、`ttft n` 样本数、`tok/s` 均值、`tps n` 样本数。 - **缺延迟键的老行不计入延迟统计**，绝不当成 0ms —— 一个 0 会把均值静默拉低，报出一个从未观测到的「变快」。`ttft_ms` 真的等于 0 是合法样本，「没有这个键」是另一件事，两者不能混。 - `p50` 用 **nearest-rank**，不做插值：偶数样本的插值中位数是任何一次请求都没产生过的数字，这份报表只印实测值。 - 样本 <3 时在 `ttft n` 后打 `*`（一两行的均值不是趋势）；某组某个指标没样本打 `-`；整次选择都没有延迟样本时打一行诚实的空态文案，而不是一片 0。 - 垃圾值（`"abc"`、`NaN`、`Infinity`、负数 ttft、0 tok/s）进不了统计，报表里永远不会出现 `NaN` / `Infinity`。 本机实测（2026-11-25，真实账本 221 条，`node scripts/query-cost.mjs`，退出码 0）节选： ``` failure rate (per route): route calls failed fail% workbuddy/deepseek-v4-pro 3 0 0.0% evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# Coding Documentation Standard

Author: Perijn Huijser

A clean, bundle-loaded DeepSeek Harness plugin that blocks undocumented pending
source and Docker Compose writes, while reserving detailed formatter and static
analysis checks for `verify`.

## Design

The package manifest declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, which points to
`bundle.patch.yml`. That patch is the only Cordis loader content this package
supplies. Registration itself belongs to `dsh plugin`, which owns the dependency
spec, the lockfile, the installed package link, and the profile's ordered
`dsh.profile.bundles` entry. This package's installer provisions the pinned
toolchain and the machine-wide skill only — it writes no package link and
**never changes a profile's `cordis.patch.yml`**.

```text
bundle.patch.yml → host plugin ──── durable policy in ~/.dsh/plugins/
                     │
                     └─ async tools/pre-execute
                          ├─ formatting          pinned formatter
                          ├─ documentation       Python header checker
                          ├─ public units        JSDoc and doc comments
                          ├─ tree-sitter         declared units, 12 languages
                          └─ project adapter     optional native tool
                          ▲ concurrent, one shared budget, one aggregated answer
```

## How enforcement behaves

The gate is asynchronous and never blocks the host. All applicable checks for one
pending write run concurrently under a single budget (`validatorTimeoutMs`,
20000 ms by default), so one round trip reveals the whole picture instead of
one problem at a time.

- **One denial, every finding.** A blocked write returns a single message: the
  issue count, the numbered findings, the formatter pointer when formatting is
  involved, and the rule reference to read.
- **Nothing is blocked on a check that could not run.** An unreadable file, an
  ambiguous `old_string` match, an oversized candidate, or a pattern on the
  ignore list means the write is skipped, not denied. If the budget expires, the
  write is allowed with a visible notice unless you set `validatorFailOpen` to
  `false`. Findings that were already found still deny, with a
  `Not fully checked: …` trailer.
- **Vendored, generated, minified, and lockfile paths are never blocked.**
  `ignoredPaths` adds to those defaults; it cannot remove them.
- **The rules are stated up front.** A short, always-on system-prompt section
  tells the agent to read the language reference in the
  `coding-doc-standard` skill and to put the documentation in the same draft
  as the code. Turn it off with `systemPromptAdvisory: false`.
- **Widening coverage is a setting.** `matchedTools` accepts extra tool names,
  including globs such as `mcp__*__write_file`, for write paths beyond the
  bundled names.

For source edits, use `edit_formatted` with `file_path`, `old_string`,
`new_string`, and `language`; optional `replace_all` replaces every match, and
`formatter_args` forwards formatter options. It applies the edit in memory,
formats the whole file, checks documentation, then commits through the native
edit tool. Missing or ambiguous matches and failed checks prevent writing; a
change that invalidates the original snapshot is refused instead of overwritten.

Use `write_formatted` for complete-file writes and `format_code` for a read-only
preview. Both formatted write tools share the same language routing and checks.

The full knob list is in [`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md).

## Supported profiles

- Python: Ruff formatting and linting in detailed verification.
- TypeScript / JavaScript: Biome by default, or project-owned ESLint + Prettier.
- Rust: opt-in pre-write rustfmt, plus Clippy during detailed verification.
- C / C++: pinned Doxygen 1.18.0 project-level documentation verification, plus
  project-provided clang-format and clang-tidy.
- Docker Compose: comment-header documentation, pinned Prettier 3.9.6 before
  writes, plus yamllint and `docker compose config -q` during detailed verification.
- Go, C#, Java, Kotlin, Shell, PHP, Ruby, Swift, Dart, Haskell, Lua, and Scala:
  native source or module headers plus Tree-sitter-backed declaration documentation
  enabled by default. The gate checks named module declarations and direct type
  members regardless of visibility; optional project adapters can add semantic checks.

All supported documentation profiles are enabled by default and can be disabled
individually in the plugin settings. TypeScript and JavaScript routing includes
`.ts`, `.tsx`, `.mts`, `.cts`, `.js`, `.jsx`, `.mjs`, and `.cjs`.

Compose documentation uses root and service-adjacent YAML comments. It does not
require `x-...` extension fields for prose.

## Declaration naming

Profiles with a selected language style guide also block nonconforming declaration
names before writes and during detailed path verification. Diagnostics identify
the declaration, expected casing, and guide URL. Checks use syntax trees, not
text replacements; no symbols or references are renamed.

See [naming guides and coverage](docs/naming.md) for checked languages, declaration
kinds, exceptions, and languages without a selected naming standard. Naming shares
the existing language/profile enable switches and generated/vendor exemptions in
the write gate. This is a casing check, not full semantic style-guide compliance.

## Install

Register the bundle with the supported DSH mechanism. It runs pnpm in the profile
directory and then reconciles `dsh.profile.bundles`, so the dependency spec, the
lockfile, the installed package link, and the loader registration all agree:

```text
dsh plugin --profile web add .
```

Relative path specs are anchored to the directory you invoke `dsh plugin` from,
not to the profile directory, so `add .` from this checkout links this package
rather than self-linking the profile.

Then provision the pinned toolchain and the machine-wide skill:

```text
node scripts/install/verify-install.mjs
node scripts/install/install.mjs
```

Restart DSH after installation so the bundle's patch layer is composed during
profile boot. Use `node scripts/install/install.mjs --dry-run` to preview its mutations.
Neither step edits a profile's `cordis.patch.yml`.

## Verify

```text
npm test
npm run verify
```

Without paths, `npm run verify` checks package completeness. Pass target paths
for detailed checks, for example `npm run verify -- compose.yaml src/main.py`.
Use `--optional` to report unavailable external tools without failing.

## Repository layout

```text
scripts/install/    installation, toolchain provisioning, install verification
scripts/verify/     detailed verifier and DSH contract checks
scripts/adapters/   bundled native public-unit adapter templates
examples/           documented demo files used for manual enforcement probes
.temp/              transient local scratch space (gitignored, never committed)
```

`client.js` stays at the package root because DSH discovers the conventional
client entry there, and `bundle.patch.yml` is the manifest-declared patch path.

## Pinned pre-write formatters

Python uses Ruff `0.16.6`; TypeScript and JavaScript use `@biomejs/biome`
`2.5.12`; and Docker Compose uses Prettier `3.9.6`. Agents call
`write_formatted` with the intended `file_path`, the complete UTF-8 `content`,
and the `language` it declares: it formats the candidate, documentation-checks
the formatted bytes, and writes them in one call, answering with a short
receipt. `format_code` runs the same cycle and never writes, so the formatted
text comes back for review instead of landing. `language` is required and must
agree with `file_path` — a `.ts` path declared as `python` is refused instead
of being formatted with the wrong parser — while a path no managed formatter
covers (`.md`, `.rs`, anything outside the table above) belongs on the plain
`write` tool, which still gates it. The destination need not exist, and the
formatter only ever reads the candidate from standard input.

Humans can invoke the same managed binaries through the slash command:

```text
/code-formatter --python --file test.py -- --line-length 100
/code-formatter --typescript --file src/main.ts
/code-formatter --javascript --file src/main.js -- --indent-style space
/code-formatter --docker-compose --file compose.yaml
```

The command formats an existing file in place by default. Add formatter-specific
`--check` after `--` for a check-only run. For a candidate that does not exist on
disk, pass its intended path with `--file` and either quoted UTF-8 source through
`--content-utf8` or Base64-encoded UTF-8 through `--content-base64`. Direct UTF-8
is convenient for simple text; Base64 is robust when source contains conflicting
quotes or command-like syntax. The formatter reads the candidate from stdin and
returns formatted source under `Output:` without creating the file. Results include
the resolved executable, arguments, workspace, exit status, and formatter output.
See `docs/toolchain.md` for provisioning, settings controls, and why Rust and C++
remain detailed-only.

## Public-unit adapters

TypeScript and JavaScript can opt into direct-export JSDoc checks. Python also
checks known parameter and return sections on documented public functions. Rust
and C/C++ can opt into the bundled native-tool adapters: rustdoc enforces Rust's
`missing_docs` lint, while C/C++ supports explicitly configured project-owned
native adapters. Doxygen remains available for detailed project verification. Configure them using [`docs/public-unit-adapters.md`](docs/public-unit-adapters.md).
The adapter receives pending candidate text without disk staging and native tools
remain responsible for resolving the project's actual public surface.

The evidence and remaining design decisions for language-specific adapters are in
[`docs/plans/language-profile-expansion.md`](docs/plans/language-profile-expansion.md).
Elixir remains deferred until an AST-aware `@moduledoc` / `@doc` adapter exists.

Native hooks can format/write files and run configurable adapters. validatorFailOpen is an explicit configurable policy, not a safety proof. No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.

# dsh-plugin-reactive-resume Connect [Reactive Resume](https://rxresu.me) to [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). Read, create, and edit your resumes and job applications from a Harness session. ## Install ```bash dsh plugin --profile add dsh-plugin-reactive-resume ``` This package declares `dsh.bundle`, so the profile picks it up as a layer and mounts it automatically. Until you configure a key it mounts nothing and logs a warning, so installing it never leaves a profile unbootable. ## Configure Mint an API key at `https://rxresu.me/dashboard/settings/api-keys` and export it as `RXRESUME_API_KEY` — the bundle patch reads that variable. To set it explicitly, or to change any other option, patch the row by id from your profile's `cordis.patch.yml`: ```yaml - id: reactive-resume config: apiKey: !!js process.env.RXRESUME_API_KEY ``` ### Options | Key | Default | Description | | ------------------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | `apiKey` | `''` | API key from `/dashboard/settings/api-keys`. Empty mounts nothing. | | `url` | `https://rxresu.me` | Origin of your instance. Set this if you self-host. | | `serverName` | `resume` | Tool namespace. Tools reach the model as `mcp____`. | | `toolCallTimeoutMs` | `60000` | Per-tool-call timeout. | Every tool Reactive Resume publishes is exposed. Narrowing that set is not currently possible from a plugin: Harness's `ctx.tools.restrict()` requires an agent-scoped context, which a plugin context is not. ### Self-hosted ```yaml - id: reactive-resume config: apiKey: !!js process.env.RXRESUME_API_KEY url: http://localhost:3000 ``` ## What it does Bridges Reactive Resume's MCP server into `ctx.tools`, and contributes a system-prompt section covering the things models get wrong about resume editing: reading before patching, RFC 6902 path construction against the published schema, UUID-keyed section entries, and locked resumes. You could wire the bridge yourself with a raw `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` row. What you cannot do that way is contribute the prompt section — that is what this package adds. ## Harness compatibility The peer ranges list each supported DSH host line as an explicit `||` union: `^0.1.0-rc.6` (what this package already shipped against) plus `^0.2.0-rc.1` (which admits `0.2.0-rc.1` and `0.2.0-rc.2`). The union is purely additive — every version the old range admitted is still admitted. Every published DSH release is a prerelease, which makes the comparison mode matter: - The Harness host decides whether to mount a plugin with `semver.satisfies(runtime, range, { includePrerelease: true })`. The upper bound is what rejected the old range there: `^0.1.0-rc.6` expands to `>=0.1.0-rc.6 <0.2.0-0`, and `0.2.0-rc.2` sorts above `0.2.0-0` because the numeric identifier `0` precedes `rc`. - npm's default mode — the one the plugin market's checker uses — additionally requires a comparator set to pin the same `major.minor.patch` tuple with a prerelease of its own. Under that mode the bare `^0.1.0-rc.6` admits only `0.1.0-rc.6` through `0.1.0-rc.8`. Measured against all 29 published host releases, that gap is wide: `^0.1.0-rc.6` admits 22 of them under the host's mode (every `0.1.x` line, including `0.1.5-rc.2` and `0.1.7-rc.2`) but only 3 under npm's default mode. Widening the upper bound does not close it, because the default mode ignores the widened comparator: `>=0.1.0-rc.6 <0.3.0-0` still admits only those same 3, and `*` admits none at all. `^0.1.0-rc.6 || ^0.2.0-rc.1` admits 24 releases under the host's mode and 5 under the default one, so an explicit union member per host line is the only form both checkers agree on. Against `0.2.0-rc.2` this package needed no source change: `dsh-mcp-client@0.2.0-rc.2` keeps its `Config` union, its `apply(ctx, config)` signature, and the `mcp____` public tool name, while `dsh-system-prompt@0.2.0-rc.2` keeps `section({ name, order, text })`. What 0.2.0 adds to the bridge — MCP resource publishing and a server-instructions prompt section — is additive and scoped to `ctx.inject(["mcpResources"])` / `ctx.inject(["systemPrompt"])`, neither of which this package depends on. ## Development This package lives in the [Reactive Resume monorepo](https://github.com/reactive-resume/reactive-resume) at `packages/dsh-plugin`, next to `packages/mcp` — the server it bridges. `src/tool-names.test.ts` checks every tool the prompt guide names against `@reactive-resume/mcp/tool-names`, so renaming a tool breaks this package in the same pull request. ```bash pnpm --filter dsh-plugin-reactive-resume test pnpm --filter dsh-plugin-reactive-resume build ``` ## License MIT

Reactive Resume

Reactive Resume is a free and open-source resume builder for writing resumes and cover letters, checking your work, and tracking job applications.

Get Started · Learn More

Sponsored by

Optional AI features use a provider you connect; hosting and provider usage may have their own costs. ![Reactive Resume v6 editor with Write, Design, and Check modes and a live PDF preview](docs/images/getting-started/editor-overview.webp) ## Build a better resume, together [Join the Reactive Resume community on Discord](https://discord.gg/u9pAd3za9t) to exchange resume feedback, get help using or self-hosting the app, and share ideas with other users and contributors. - **Resume feedback:** post a redacted resume and one specific question, or help someone improve theirs. - **Help:** find troubleshooting discussions and ask questions in dedicated forum threads. - **Contribute:** discuss ideas, translations, and code with the people building Reactive Resume. Feedback comes from fellow community members. Remove contact details and other private information before posting. ## Features **Write, Design, and Check** - Redesigned editor with inline content editing and click-to-select on the page - Live PDF preview and browser downloads powered by Forme, rendered in a background worker - Rich text, custom sections, drag-and-drop ordering, and structured dates with consistent formatting - Autosave, local recovery of unsaved resume drafts, and up to 200 undo steps - Phone and tablet layouts, keyboard shortcuts, and a searchable command bar **Templates and Customization** - 18 templates, including the new Porygon and Smeargle, previewed with your own content - One-column, two-column, and ATS-safe template filters - Font presets, custom fonts, colors, spacing, A4 and Letter paper, and left or right sidebars - Fit overflowing content by adjusting density, margins, and text size - Custom Styles written as Semantic CSS, with an element picker on the page **Resume Checks** - Readability checks with findings pinned to the relevant lines - Job-posting keyword matching and a view of the text hiring software reads - Checks on the exported PDF, plus an optional AI writing review - A public [ATS checker](https://rxresu.me/ats-checker) that reads PDFs in your browser without an account **Documents and Cover Letters** - One searchable library for resumes and letters, with tags, sorting, and grid or list views - Standalone cover letters with their own editor, exports, and version history - Link a letter to a resume to keep its sender details and design in sync, or customize it independently - Automatic and named versions you can preview and restore - Trash with Undo and a 30-day recovery window **Job Applications** - List, Board, Insights, and Calendar views for tracking applications from Saved to Offer - Save jobs from a URL or pasted posting; optional keyword search through Firecrawl, Tavily, or Exa - Tailor a resume and draft a cover letter for a saved job - Track contacts, notes, follow-ups, application outcomes, and the documents you sent - Schedule interviews, export calendar events, and import or export applications as CSV **AI Assistant** - Assistant beside your resume or letter, with conversations tied to that document - Proposed edits show what changes and why; accept or reject each suggestion - Improve selected text, review writing, and draft letters from a resume and job posting - Connect OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, OpenRouter, Ollama, or other supported providers and compatible endpoints - Optional web search and page reading; self-hosters can configure shared AI and web-access providers **Import, Export, and Sharing** - Import Reactive Resume JSON, JSON Resume, LinkedIn data exports, PDF, and Word files - JSON, LinkedIn, and readable PDF imports work without AI; Word imports require a connected provider - Export resumes and letters as PDF, Word (DOCX), Markdown, or JSON - Share resumes through public links with optional password protection and view/download statistics - REST API and MCP server for document management, imports, exports, checks, and application workflows **Privacy and Control** - Self-host with Docker, Vercel, Cloudflare Workers, or a 1-click deploy on Hostinger - No tracking or ads; export your account data or delete your account - Passkeys, two-factor authentication, and linked sign-in providers - Multiple interface languages, light/dark/system themes, and reduced-motion support ## Templates

For a deployment using published images, follow the [Docker guide](https://docs.rxresu.me/self-hosting/docker). For source development, see the [development setup guide](https://docs.rxresu.me/contributing/development). ## Tech Stack | Category | Technology | | ---------------- | ---------------------------------------- | | Web app | React 19 SPA, TanStack Router, and Vite | | Server | Hono on Node.js 26 or Cloudflare Workers | | Language | TypeScript | | Monorepo | pnpm and Turborepo | | Database | PostgreSQL with Drizzle ORM | | API | oRPC, OpenAPI REST, and MCP | | Auth | Better Auth | | Styling | Tailwind CSS | | UI Components | Base UI + shared UI package | | State Management | Zustand + TanStack Query | | PDF rendering | Forme, with PDF.js for the viewer | | Rich text | TipTap | | Localization | Lingui | ## Documentation The full documentation lives at [docs.rxresu.me](https://docs.rxresu.me): | Guide | Description | | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | | [Getting started](https://docs.rxresu.me/getting-started) | First-time setup and basic usage | | [What's new in v6](https://docs.rxresu.me/guides/whats-new-in-v6) | Changes and where familiar features moved | | [Checking your resume](https://docs.rxresu.me/guides/checking-your-resume) | Readability, job match, and writing reviews | | [Using the assistant](https://docs.rxresu.me/guides/using-the-assistant) | Ask for changes and review proposed edits | | [Resume and career agent skills](plugins/reactive-resume/README.md) | 32 skills for resume writing, specific roles and the job search | | [Writing a cover letter](https://docs.rxresu.me/guides/writing-a-cover-letter) | Create a letter and link it to a resume | | [Tracking job applications](https://docs.rxresu.me/guides/tracking-job-applications) | Saved jobs, stages, interviews, and insights | | [Exporting your resume](https://docs.rxresu.me/guides/exporting-your-resume) | PDF, Word, Markdown, and JSON downloads | | [API](https://docs.rxresu.me/guides/using-the-api) and [MCP](https://docs.rxresu.me/guides/using-the-mcp-server) | Connect scripts and external assistants | | [Self-hosting](https://docs.rxresu.me/self-hosting/docker) | Deploy on your own infrastructure | | [Migrating from v5](https://docs.rxresu.me/self-hosting/upgrading-to-v6) | Migrations and integration changes | | [Development setup](https://docs.rxresu.me/contributing/development) | Local development environment | | [Project architecture](https://docs.rxresu.me/contributing/architecture) | Codebase structure and package boundaries | ## Self-Hosting Reactive Resume runs the same application everywhere: PostgreSQL for data, plus storage for uploads. Pick the option that fits how much you want to manage. | Option | Best for | Guide | | ----------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | [Hostinger](#hostinger) | A ready-made VPS with no setup | [Hostinger guide](https://docs.rxresu.me/self-hosting/hostinger) | | [Vercel](#vercel) | Serverless, with managed database and storage | [Vercel guide](https://docs.rxresu.me/self-hosting/vercel) | | [Cloudflare Workers](#cloudflare-workers) | Workers, R2 and your own PostgreSQL | [Cloudflare guide](https://docs.rxresu.me/self-hosting/cloudflare) | | [Docker and Kubernetes](#docker-and-kubernetes) | Your own server, homelab or cluster | [Docker](https://docs.rxresu.me/self-hosting/docker) · [Kubernetes](https://docs.rxresu.me/self-hosting/kubernetes) | > **PDF generation in v6** uses Forme in the browser and on the server. No Browserless, Chromium, or external print service is needed. Legacy `PRINTER_*` and `BROWSERLESS_*` environment variables can be removed. ### Hostinger The quickest way to get going is a 1-click deploy on Hostinger, starting at $6.49/month. Their VPS plans include a ready-made Reactive Resume template that provisions the Docker environment and brings the app up for you, with weekly backups and a Docker manager UI included — so you can skip the setup entirely. See the [Hostinger guide](https://docs.rxresu.me/self-hosting/hostinger) for what the template sets up and what to configure afterwards, such as email, your own domain, and turning off sign-ups. ### Vercel [![Deploy with Vercel](https://vercel.com/button)](https://vercel.com/new/clone?repository-url=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Freactive-resume%2Freactive-resume&project-name=reactive-resume&repository-name=reactive-resume&env=AUTH_SECRET%2CENCRYPTION_SECRET&envDescription=Generate+two+independent+secrets+with+openssl+rand+-hex+32.+Keep+these+values+across+deployments.&envLink=https%3A%2F%2Fdocs.rxresu.me%2Fself-hosting%2Fvercel&stores=%5B%7B%22type%22%3A%22integration%22%2C%22protocol%22%3A%22storage%22%2C%22integrationSlug%22%3A%22neon%22%2C%22productSlug%22%3A%22neon%22%7D%2C%7B%22type%22%3A%22integration%22%2C%22protocol%22%3A%22storage%22%2C%22integrationSlug%22%3A%22upstash%22%2C%22productSlug%22%3A%22upstash-kv%22%7D%2C%7B%22type%22%3A%22blob%22%2C%22access%22%3A%22private%22%7D%5D) Vercel provisions Neon PostgreSQL, private Blob storage, and Upstash Redis through its deployment wizard. Supply two persistent secrets and use the **Services** framework preset. Static assets run in the frontend service, and Hono serves the application routes and APIs from the backend service. See the [Vercel guide](https://docs.rxresu.me/self-hosting/vercel) for setup, limits, and optional SMTP/OAuth configuration. ### Cloudflare Workers Cloudflare deployment requires **Workers Paid** and uses Static Assets, private R2 storage, SQLite Durable Objects, and PostgreSQL through Hyperdrive. Supply an existing PostgreSQL database and apply migrations before deployment. See the [Cloudflare guide](https://docs.rxresu.me/self-hosting/cloudflare) for setup and runtime limits. ### Docker and Kubernetes The application needs: - **PostgreSQL** — Accounts, documents, applications, and assistant conversations - **Upload storage** — A persistent local directory or an S3-compatible bucket, such as SeaweedFS - **Redis** (optional) — Shared coordination across instances and resumable assistant replies - **SMTP** (optional) — Verification and password-reset emails Published releases are available from Docker Hub and GitHub Container Registry (`latest` tracks the latest stable release): ```bash # Docker Hub docker pull amruthpillai/reactive-resume:latest # GitHub Container Registry docker pull ghcr.io/reactive-resume/reactive-resume:latest ``` See the [Docker guide](https://docs.rxresu.me/self-hosting/docker) or [Kubernetes guide](https://docs.rxresu.me/self-hosting/kubernetes) for complete instructions. Running on a NAS? See the [Synology and UGREEN guides](https://docs.rxresu.me/self-hosting/nas). ### Configuration Every setting is listed in the [environment variables reference](https://docs.rxresu.me/self-hosting/environment-variables). Self-hosters can also configure [shared AI and job-search services](https://docs.rxresu.me/self-hosting/job-search-and-ai) and [single sign-on](https://docs.rxresu.me/self-hosting/sso). ### Upgrading from v5 Back up your database and uploads and stop all v5 instances before applying v6 migrations. Old visual style rules require a manual conversion; API and MCP integrations also have changes. Follow [Migrating from v5](https://docs.rxresu.me/self-hosting/upgrading-to-v6). ## Support Reactive Resume is and always will be free and open source. If it has helped you land a job or saved you time, please consider supporting continued development:

Other ways to support: - Star this repository - Report reproducible bugs and suggest actionable features - Help other users in [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/reactive-resume/reactive-resume/discussions/categories/q-a) - Improve documentation - Help with translations ## Star History ## Contributing Every contribution helps, whether it is a typo fix or a new feature. 1. Fork the repository 2. Create a feature branch (`git checkout -b feature/amazing-feature`) 3. Commit your changes using Conventional Commits (`git commit -m 'feat: add amazing feature'`) 4. Push to the branch (`git push origin feature/amazing-feature`) 5. Open a Pull Request See the [development setup guide](https://docs.rxresu.me/contributing/development) for how to run the project locally. evidence.readmeExcerpt:
dsh-better-edit

High-precision, hash-anchored file editing for DeepSeek Harness (dsh).
Replaces fragile line numbers and token-wasting code echoes with content-addressed line hashes — 0 silent miswrites, 0 token re-reads.

English · 简体中文

Why You Need It • Core Pillars • Quick Start • Tools • Benchmark • How Anchors Work • Development

--- > **What is `dsh-better-edit`?** > A high-precision file editing plugin for [DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai) that replaces volatile line numbers and token-wasting code echoes with immutable, content-addressed 3-character line hashes (`szJ│code`). > > **Core Philosophy:** Local compute is free; **the model's context window is the most precious resource**. By shifting verification, snapshotting, and alignment to the host, `dsh-better-edit` slashes output tokens by 40–60%, auto-rebases external file drift (e.g., Prettier, Git), and eliminates silent miswrites without forcing full-file re-reads. --- ## Why You Need It ### The 3 Fatal Editing Traps of Autonomous Coding Agents File editing is the #1 point of failure for autonomous agents. Traditional tools break down in three distinct ways: | Fatal Trap in Traditional Tools | Why It Breaks Agents | How `dsh-better-edit` Solves It | | ------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **`str_replace` Token Bleed** | Must re-type 30+ lines of unchanged code just to change 1 line ($O(S+R)$), burning expensive output tokens (billed ~5–6× input). | **$O(R)$ Payloads**: Sends only two 3-char hashes (`anchor_from`, `anchor_to`) + replacement. Cuts output tokens by 40–60%. | | **Line-Number Coordinate Rot** | Inserting 1 line shifts all line numbers below it. Agents suffer off-by-one errors or must repeatedly re-read the file. | **Position-Independent Anchors**: Line hashes follow content, not line coordinates. Exterior shifts auto-rebase cleanly. | | **Silent Miswrites & Drift** | Duplicate lines match the wrong function; external formatters (Prettier) or git updates cause blind overwrites or fatal errors. | **Content-Addressed Line Verification**: anchors derive from raw line bytes, unique via coprime probing; a re-indent survives through the lease; interior whitespace significant; fail-closed reject-and-serve. | --- ## Core Pillars ### 1. 🪙 Token Economics (40–60% Context Savings) - **$O(R)$ Edit Payloads**: The model emits only `{ "path": "...", "edits": [["a1b", "c3d", "..."]] }`, never echoing existing code. - **Self-Serving Diffs**: Every applied edit returns fresh anchors in the post-edit diff — zero re-read roundtrips to chain edits. - **Zero-Token Auto-Rebase**: Non-conflicting exterior shifts resolve locally without agent intervention — 0 tokens, 0 retries. - **Atomic Multi-Item Batches**: Apply up to 32 same-file edits in one tool call; overlapping spans abort atomically (`[E_BATCH_ABORT]`) before touching disk. ### 2. 🛡️ Resistance to External Writes (Drift & Concurrency) - **Edge-Whitespace Tolerance**: Anchors derive from the line's raw bytes; the alignment digest trims one leading and one trailing whitespace run. A re-indent or trailing-space strip keeps the held anchor valid through the lease (the spelling rotates with the bytes, the lease does not); interior whitespace — inside string literals too — is significant, and a change to it rejects fail-closed. - **Exterior Shift Auto-Rebase**: External edits, git checkouts, or background processes outside the edit span rebase seamlessly without agent intervention. - **Fail-Closed Reject-and-Serve**: Contested interior spans fail closed without disk corruption and immediately return fresh on-disk rows in the error (`[E_STALE_RANGE]`, `[E_UNSERVED_RANGE]`) — those rows are **recorded as served** (rows, canons, snapshot and leases, exactly like a `read` of those lines), so retry needs no `read`. Two exceptions keep the report honest: a refusal raised after an earlier item of the same call already changed the temporary buffer shows no rows and names the current-file lines an anchored read would serve, and a window whose echoed anchor the served mirror already holds elsewhere is not recorded and says so. - **Session-Keyed Leases**: Leases are isolated per session, preventing cross-agent race conditions or state pollution. ### 3. 🎯 Zero Silent Miswrites - **Decoupled Line Identity**: Lines are verified against served snapshot lineage, not ephemeral line coordinates. - **Collision-Free Anchors**: Coprime bitset probing ensures duplicate lines in a file receive distinct, unambiguous 3-character hashes. - **No Heuristic Guessing**: Retires fuzzy matching. If an anchor cannot be unambiguously resolved, it fails closed safely. - **Persisted Undo**: `undo_last_edit` restores the previous content at the **effective EOL** as UTF-8 (BOM and original anchors too, persisting across session restarts). A pre-edit mixture of line endings is **not** restored — the revert writes one ending and says so; a migrated legacy file comes back as UTF-8 text — the revert names the abandoned codec and its BOM, but the original bytes do not come back. --- > _"The harness — not the model — is the bottleneck."_ — Can Bölük, [_The Harness Problem_](https://stencil.so/blog/the-harness-problem) > > **3 calls vs 6 · -55.8% tokens · 23/23 correctness.** Tested on realistic external-drift refactoring against OMP wrapper. Payload numbers are deterministic — see [Benchmark](#benchmark). ## Quick Start — install to verified edit in 30s ### Install (pick one) ```sh npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web add github:Rianico/dsh-better-edit # from github npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-better-edit # from npm npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web add /path/to/dsh-better-edit # local ``` No config. Next session runs with hashline tools. Verify: ```sh dsh --profile --dump-config # shows "# == dsh-better-edit" layer ``` | Requirement | | | ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Node | `>=24` (per `engines.node`; a newer dsh host may require a higher minimum) | | Profile | `dsh` profile (`dsh plugin` creates one) | | Backends | sandboxed / remote `ctx.fs` | | dsh | `0.2.1-rc.2` (verified end-to-end; `0.1.6-alpha.2` was the last pre-0.2 baseline) | **dsh 0.2.0+ is supported.** Registration uses `agent/created`, path resolution follows the session's live working directory (`workingDirectory`, with the session header as the pre-0.2.1 fallback), and tool-guidance order comes from `systemPrompt.getSectionOrder`. There is no peer range and no runtime version probing: compatibility comes from that stable surface plus optional-service fallbacks, so a composition that omits `workingDirectory` or `agentPresets` keeps working. ### See it work `read` serves `HASH│content` — the hash _is_ the address: ```text ve7│function hello() { szJ│ console.log("world"); kQm│} ``` `edit` by hashes — always lands where you meant: ```json { "path": "src/main.ts", "edits": [["szJ", "szJ", " console.log('hi');"]] } ``` Returns a diff with fresh anchors — next edit needs no `read`: ```text - szJ │ console.log("world"); + a3m │ console.log('hi'); kQm │ } ``` Under `hint` mode a removed row this session never served renders the empty gutter (`- │content`) instead of an anchor, and a folded deletion appends ` (N unserved)` to its `[N lines deleted]` marker — the diff never hands back an anchor the session cannot honour. **Position-free in one line:** `read 1..5` → `insert @0` → `edit 10..12` still verifies `10..12` (`resist` mode). **Multi-session honesty:** `A:10..12+1` shifts `B:20..30→21..31` → `B` passes (drift notice); `B:12..13` overlapping `A` → `E_STALE_RANGE` + fresh rows, one retry. Batch atomically — one `edit`, up to 32 same-file ranges: ```json { "path": "src/main.ts", "edits": [ ["a1b", "a1b", "new line 1\n"], ["c3d", "c3d", "new line 2"] ] } ``` One fails → none write (`[E_BATCH_ABORT]`). > [!TIP] > **Want proof before you install?** Upstream [23/23 battery](https://github.com/Rianico/pi-better-edit/blob/main/benchmarks/README.md) runs no LLM — stale edits are rejected every run. Same algorithm. ### Configuration Tenancy and prompt guidance declare once, read at `agent/created`, no code change. **Store** central by default `$DSH_HOME/plugins/dsh-better-edit/runtime/-/` (`ls`-readable + `.wsPath` sidecar). DBs are disposable caches — `rm -rf runtime/-/` is safe, rebuilt on next `read`. ```yaml # $DSH_HOME/plugins/dsh-better-edit/config.yaml storeDir: central # central | workspace | /abs autoGitignore: false spanMode: hint # hint | strict — strict refuses an interior line never served (audit/CI) eol: AUTO # AUTO (file's dominant, then OS) | LF | CRLF | CR — LF for .gitattributes repos undo_ttl_s: 604800 # 7d, -1 forever storeMaxAgeS: 2592000 # 30d janitor storeMaxTotalBytes: 524288000 # 500 MB LRU ``` Env overrides yaml (`DSH_BETTER_EDIT_STORE_DIR`, `DSH_BETTER_EDIT_AUTO_GITIGNORE`, `DSH_BETTER_EDIT_SPAN_MODE=hint|strict`, `DSH_BETTER_EDIT_EOL`). **Store lifetime** — the store closes itself. The last agent to detach releases its workspace's handle: synchronously when nothing is in flight, after the in-flight work drains otherwise. A workspace shared with another agent stays open while any agent still holds it. Closing deletes no data — undo history survives, so a resumed session can still `undo_last_edit`. A host that must free a directory calls `releaseHashStore(cwd?: string, options?: { force?: boolean }): Promise`: a graceful release refuses (`false`) while an agent holds the path and otherwise drains and closes; `force` clears the claims, drains and closes; omit `cwd` to target every open store. It returns `true` only when every targeted path settled its drain and closed. Another agent or an in-flight operation keeps the store open, so deleting the workspace or runtime-cache directory stays blocked until the last claim's close; call force-release only when no new store calls will start, and expect a load that overlaps a release to reject with `hash store: released while the store was opening`. See [ADR-0057](docs/adr/0057-session-scoped-per-workspace-store-lifecycle.md). **Span mode** — `strict` for audit, CI or review sessions where an unreviewed interior must never be replaced; `hint` for interactive work where the model usually knows the span it replaces. `hint` (the default) applies the edit and discloses it with `[W_UNSERVED_INTERIOR]`, naming the replaced file-line count, the unserved count and the exact absolute file lines as compressed runs; `strict` refuses before any write with a rowless `[E_UNSERVED_RANGE]` carrying the same facts. One formatter owns both voices, so their grammar and list compression cannot drift ([ADR-0053](docs/adr/0053-unserved-interior-one-formatter.md)). No per-call override — the profile owns the policy. See [ADR-0045](docs/adr/0045-strict-span-mode.md). **Line endings** — every `edit` writes **one** effective EOL, resolved `DSH_BETTER_EDIT_EOL` > `eol` (config) > the file's dominant terminator (whole file; ties prefer LF, then CRLF, then CR) > the system ending (`\r\n` on Windows, `\n` elsewhere). `AUTO` follows the file's dominant ending, and a file that spells **no** terminator falls back to **the system ending** — so the same edit writes `\r\n` on a Windows host and `\n` on a Linux host. Set `eol: LF` in cross-platform repositories that rely on `.gitattributes` and need one spelling on every host; `LF`/`CRLF`/`CR` force that ending. A file that mixes endings says so on read — `[W_MIXED_EOL] Mixed EOL: 2 CRLF, 1 LF. All edits normalize to CRLF (file).` — and an edit that re-spells terminators reports `[MODEL] [W_EOL_REWRITTEN] EOL normalized to CRLF (file): 1 terminators changed. Undo restores normalized content.` `undo_last_edit` restores at that same effective EOL and names it when a pre-edit mixture could not come back. **File encoding** — a `read` records the file's `{encoding, hasBOM}` and a later write must reproduce those bytes through a text-only seam that always encodes UTF-8. A legacy file that cannot round-trip (UTF-16, or `windows-1251` with non-ASCII content) therefore refuses with `[E_ENCODING_UNWRITABLE]` — nothing is written, nothing is silently transcoded, and the served anchors still describe the bytes on disk. A conversion needs an explicit consent and a UTF-8 target, and the default is `refuse`: name `allow_encoding_migration: "utf8"` or `"utf8bom"` on the `edit` payload for one call, or set the standing `allowEncodingMigration` setting (`refuse | utf8 | utf8bom`) in `$DSH_HOME/plugins/dsh-better-edit/config.yaml` (env override: `DSH_BETTER_EDIT_ALLOW_ENCODING_MIGRATION`); the legacy `normalizeToUtf8: true` is still honoured as `"utf8"`. `"utf8"` writes the migrated file without a BOM; `"utf8bom"` writes one leading `EF BB BF`, which BOM-aware readers decode as UTF-8. The conversion is a one-way door the applied result carries as `[W_ENCODING_MIGRATED]` and the revert names but never reverses (`undo_last_edit` restores the text as UTF-8 — behind the target's BOM after a `"utf8bom"` migration — while the original codec and its BOM are gone). Reopen bytes under another codec with `read({ encoding })` (e.g. `windows-1251`); the `autoGuessEncoding` gate (`DSH_BETTER_EDIT_AUTO_GUESS_ENCODING`, default `false`) auto-decodes only after deterministic BOM → strict-UTF-8 detection fails: a guess it is not confident about is reported on the read together with its Top-3 candidates, and a file it cannot decode is refused with the Top-3 for the model to pick from. Guessing ranges over `supportedEncodings` (`DSH_BETTER_EDIT_SUPPORTED_ENCODINGS`, default `gbk, big5, shift_jis, euc-kr, windows-1251, iso-8859-1`); UTF-8 is always accepted outside that list — the deterministic BOM → strict-UTF-8 pass runs before any guessing. An ASCII-only file under a legacy name is byte-faithful and edits silently at every consent — its bytes are already UTF-8 and no BOM is added. **Guidance per preset** — `tool:read` / `tool:edit` / `tool:undo_last_edit` are plain markdown per preset at `$DSH_HOME/plugins/dsh-better-edit//
.md`. The default order is the harness's own tool slot (`systemPrompt.getSectionOrder`: `1100` read, `1300` edit, `1310` undo), so a band change upstream moves the sections with it. A fresh install seeds the shipped presets — `standard`, `ptc`, `minimal`, `cordis` — with the compiled default body and writes **no** `order:` fence; a hand-written `order` front-matter still pins a custom position. An unmodified seeded file refreshes itself when a release changes the compiled default, while a file you edited is preserved byte-identically and listed in one boot warning — together with any stale or customized file in a custom preset. A deliberate blank (`---\n---\n`) is preserved silently. Delete or empty a file → the default re-seeds at next boot. A local override that diverges from the default appends the `[USER] [W_PROMPT_DIVERGED]` footer to its section text. See [ADR-0052](docs/adr/0052-guidance-seed-provenance-and-upgrade-lifecycle.md). ## Why Hashline **Verified against what was served.** Every line the session has served evidence for is checked against `read`/diff/rejection rows. The two **boundary** anchors must still resolve, but a boundary pair does not prove the model saw the lines between them: on the leased route it can authorize a span across unserved **interior** lines, so a never-served line is not by itself a refusal (`hint` discloses the replaced interior; `spanMode: strict` refuses it). Read one contiguous range when the interior matters. A stale boundary → `[E_STALE_RANGE]`/`[E_UNSERVED_RANGE]` + fresh `HASH│content` recorded as served, so the retry needs no `read`; a refusal that shows no rows (a changed batch buffer, `[E_TARGET_LOST]`, an unresolved anchor) records nothing and names the read. Session-scoped — sub-agent serves never validate main edits. **Content-addressed.** The anchor is `xxh32` over the line's raw bytes → `62³=238,328` anchors, while `canon(line)` — one leading and one trailing whitespace run trimmed — is the alignment digest that pairs snapshots and verifies served evidence. Re-inserting identical text keeps its hash; a re-indent or trailing-space pass between edits rotates the spelling but not the lease, so the held anchor keeps working. Interior whitespace is significant — `"a b"` and `"ab"` are different lines, even inside a string literal. Unique by bitset probing — `}`/`import` repeats never collide; cap `238,328` lines (`[E_LARGE_FILE]`). **No loop, no ritual.** No-op → `No changes made`; same no-op ×3 → `[E_NOOP_LOOP]`. Diff and row-carrying rejection rows count as serves — only a rowless refusal names a `read`, and `read` is recovery, not ritual. ### Token economics Envelope change: hoist `path`, `edits:[[from,to,text]]`, never repeat `old_string`. | snapshot | `str_replace` | `edit` | `edit` multi | OMP per-edit | OMP batch | | --------------------- | ------------: | -------------: | -------------: | -------------: | -------------: | | pinned 12-edit corpus | 1,015 | 609 **-40.0%** | 582 **-42.7%** | 590 **-41.9%** | 480 **-52.7%** | | local snapshot | 358 | 272 **-24.0%** | 241 **-32.7%** | 268 **-25.1%** | 180 **-49.7%** | Percent vs `str_replace`. External row pinned corpus, `cl100k_base`; local `npm run benchmark` in upstream. | engine | calls | tokens | saved | ok | | --------------- | ----: | -----: | ---------: | :-: | | OMP | **6** | 28,467 | — | ✅ | | hashline `edit` | **3** | 12,593 | **-55.8%** | ✅ | Single stochastic run, `opencode-go/gpt-5.6-luna` high. [Artifact](https://github.com/Rianico/pi-better-edit/blob/main/benchmarks/results/2026-08-17-practical-token-benchmark.md). > **Scope & honesty.** Payload deterministic; practical run stochastic. We measure **payload + round-trips**, not throughput. Retries are where the gap is largest — see [edge cases](#comparison). ## Tools | Tool | What it does | | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | `read` | `HASH│content` with `offset`/`limit`; `[Showing N-M of T]` paging; `>200KB` lines show marker | | `read_skill` | Plain text, no hashes, no serves — editing after it needs a serve | | `edit` | `{file, edits:[[from,to,text]]}` (named objects too; `path`/`file_path` aliases fold), `""` deletes, atomic ≤32, verify-then-write | | `undo_last_edit` | `{path}` restores last edit at its effective EOL as UTF-8 (BOM/anchors too), names a lost mixture or a migrated codec+BOM, persisted | `write` stays, but refuses an exact `HASH│` echo for same `session/path/line` before dispatch. ### Error codes | Code | Meaning | What to do | | ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `[E_BAD_PAYLOAD]` | Request shape is wrong (unknown field, missing `file`, bad tuple) | Fix the shape and resend | | `[E_MALFORMED_ANCHOR]` | The anchor token is not a bare 3-char anchor (pasted block or pseudo-anchor) | Pass the bare anchor and retry | | `[E_UNKNOWN_ANCHOR]` | The anchor was never served for this file | `read` the file for fresh anchors | | `[E_FOREIGN_ANCHOR]` | The anchor belongs to another file or session | Use anchors served for this file | | `[E_STALE_ANCHOR]` | The anchor no longer resolves (hash / retired / canon miss) | `read` for fresh anchors | | `[E_AMBIGUOUS_MATCH]` | `str_replace` `old_str` matches more than once | Narrow `old_str` | | `[E_NO_MATCH]` | `str_replace` `old_str` is absent | Re-`view` and retry | | `[E_EMPTY_RANGE]` | The edit would empty a non-empty file | Use `write` | | `[E_STALE_RANGE]` | The served range changed on disk | Apply the echoed fresh rows (recorded as served); a rowless refusal names the `read` | | `[E_UNSERVED_RANGE]` | A boundary anchor never resolved, or — in `strict` — the span replaces interior lines never served | `hint`: use the echoed rows (recorded as served), or `read` when the refusal is rowless. `strict`: the rowless refusal names the replaced file-line count, the unserved count and the exact absolute file lines; `read` them | | `[E_UNVERIFIED_RANGE]` | A boundary anchor could not be verified against served state | `read` and retry | | `[E_SUSPICIOUS_TEXT]` | Replacement text carries copied `HASH│` or diff-preview markers | Remove them and resend | | `[E_BLIND_REPLACE]` | `write` / `str_replace_editor` ran before the file was observed | `read` / `view` first | | `[E_TARGET_LOST]` | The target vanished or changed identity mid-operation | `read` and re-target | | `[E_BATCH_ABORT]` | One or more items failed; nothing was written. The verdict reads `Batch rejected: K of N edits failed`, then one `- edits[i] (path) [E_*]:` bullet per failure | Fix each failing bullet and resend the batch | | `[E_NOOP_LOOP]` | The same no-op edit was submitted three times. A row-carrying refusal shows the range and records it as served; a changed-buffer refusal shows no rows and names the read | Change the edit, or retry with the shown anchors when rows are served | | `[E_ACCESS]` | The path is not readable or writable | Fix the permission | | `[E_NOT_FOUND]` | No such file
